hard.translation: And We have given you (mankind) power in the earth, and appointed for you therein livelihoods. Little give ye thanks!

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: He said: Then go down hence! It is not for thee to show pride here, so go forth! Lo! thou art of those degraded.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: He said: Go forth from hence, degraded, banished. As for such of them as follow thee, surely I will fill hell with all of you.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: They said: Our Lord! We have wronged ourselves. If thou forgive us not and have not mercy on us, surely we are of the lost!

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: He said: Go down (from hence), one of you a foe unto the other. There will be for you on earth a habitation and provision for a while.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: And every nation hath its term, and when its term cometh, they cannot put it off an hour nor yet advance (it).

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: But they who deny Our revelations and scorn them - each are rightful owners of the Fire; they will abide therein.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: Theirs will be a bed of hell, and over them coverings (of hell). Thus do We requite wrong-doers.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: Who debar (men) from the path of Allah and would have it crooked, and who are disbelievers in the Last Day.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: Verily We have brought them a Scripture which We expounded with knowledge, a guidance and a mercy for a people who believe.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: (O mankind!) Call upon your Lord humbly and in secret. Lo! He loveth not aggressors.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: The chieftains of his people said: Lo! we see thee surely in plain error.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: He said: O my people! There is no error in me, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the Worlds.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: I convey unto you the messages of my Lord and give good counsel unto you, and know from Allah that which ye know not.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: Marvel ye that there should come unto you a Reminder from your Lord by means of a man among you, that he may warn you, and that ye may keep from evil, and that haply ye may find mercy.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: He said: O my people! There is no foolishness in me, but I am a messenger from the Lord of the Worlds.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: And Lot! (Remember) when he said unto his folk: Will ye commit abomination such as no creature ever did before you?

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: Lo! ye come with lust unto men instead of women. Nay, but ye are wanton folk.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: And We rained a rain upon them. See now the nature of the consequence of evil-doers!

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: But the chieftains of his people, who were disbelieving, said: If ye follow Shu'eyb, then truly ye shall be the losers.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: And We sent no prophet unto any township but We did afflict its folk with tribulation and adversity that haply they might grow humble.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: Are the people of the townships then secure from the coming of Our wrath upon them as a night-raid while they sleep?

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: Or are the people of the townships then secure from the coming of Our wrath upon them in the daytime while they play?

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: Are they then secure from Allah's scheme? None deemeth himself secure from Allah's scheme save folk that perish.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: We found no (loyalty to any) covenant in most of them. Nay, most of them We found wrong-doers.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: (Pharaoh) said: If thou comest with a token, then produce it, if thou art of those who speak the truth.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: The chiefs of Pharaoh's people said: Lo! this is some knowing wizard,

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: And the wizards came to Pharaoh, saying: Surely there will be a reward for us if we are victors.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: They said: O Moses! Either throw (first) or let us be the first throwers?

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: He said: Throw! And when they threw they cast a spell upon the people's eyes, and overawed them, and produced a mighty spell.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: And We inspired Moses (saying): Throw thy staff! And lo! it swallowed up their lying show.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: And we straitened Pharaoh's folk with famine and dearth of fruits, that peradventure they might heed.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: And they said: Whatever portent thou bringest wherewith to bewitch us, we shall not put faith in thee.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: So We sent against them the flood and the locusts and the vermin and the frogs and the blood - a succession of clear signs. But they were arrogant and became a guilty folk.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: But when We did remove from them the terror for a term which they must reach, behold! they broke their covenant.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: Therefore We took retribution from them; therefore We drowned them in the sea: because they denied Our revelations and were heedless of them.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: Lo! as for these, their way will be destroyed and all that they are doing is in vain.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: He said: Shall I seek for you a god other than Allah when He hath favoured you above (all) creatures?

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: He said: My Lord! Have mercy on me and on my brother; bring us into Thy mercy, Thou the Most Merciful of all who show mercy.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: So when they took pride in that which they had been forbidden, We said unto them: Be ye apes despised and loathed!

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: And as for those who make (men) keep the Scripture, and establish worship - lo! We squander not the wages of reformers.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: Recite unto them the tale of him to whom We gave Our revelations, but he sloughed them off, so Satan overtook him and he became of those who lead astray.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: Evil as an example are the folk who denied Our revelations, and were wont to wrong themselves.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: He whom Allah leadeth, he indeed is led aright, while he whom Allah sendeth astray - they indeed are losers.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: Have they not bethought them (that) there is no madness in their comrade? He is but a plain warner.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: Those whom Allah sendeth astray, there is no guide for them. He leaveth them to wander blindly on in their contumacy.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: But when He gave unto them aright, they ascribed unto Him partners in respect of that which He had given them. High is He Exalted above all that they associate (with Him).

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: And if ye call them to the Guidance, they follow you not. Whether ye call them or are silent is all one for you.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: Lo! my Protecting Friend is Allah Who revealeth the Scripture. He befriendeth the righteous.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: They on whom ye call beside Him have no power to help you, nor can they help you, nor can they help themselves.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: And if ye (Muslims) call them to the guidance they hear not; and thou (Muhammad) seest them looking toward thee, but they see not.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: And if a slander from the devil wound thee, then seek refuge in Allah. Lo! He is Hearer, Knower.

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: Lo! those who ward off (evil), when a glamour from the devil troubleth them, they do but remember (Allah's Guidance) and behold them seers!

hard.name: Al-A'raf
hard.translation: Lo! those who are with thy Lord are not too proud to do Him service, but they praise Him and prostrate before Him.

hard.name: Al-Anfal
hard.translation: Those are they who are in truth believers. For them are grades (of honour) with their Lord, and pardon, and a bountiful provision.

hard.name: Al-Anfal
hard.translation: Even as thy Lord caused thee (Muhammad) to go forth from thy home with the Truth, and lo! a party of the believers were averse (to it).

hard.name: Al-Anfal
hard.translation: Disputing with thee of the Truth after it had been made manifest, as if they were being driven to death visible.

hard.name: Al-Anfal
hard.translation: When ye sought help of your Lord and He answered you (saying): I will help you with a thousand of the angels, rank on rank.

hard.name: Al-Anfal
hard.translation: O ye who believe! When ye meet those who disbelieve in battle, turn not your backs to them.

hard.name: Al-Anfal
hard.translation: O ye who believe! Obey Allah and His messenger, and turn not away from him when ye hear (him speak).

hard.name: Al-Anfal
hard.translation: Lo! the worst of beasts in Allah's sight are the deaf, the dumb, who have no sense.

hard.name: Al-Anfal
hard.translation: Had Allah known of any good in them He would have made them hear, but had He made them hear they would have turned away, averse.

hard.name: Al-Anfal
hard.translation: O ye who believe! Betray not Allah and His messenger, nor knowingly betray your trusts.

hard.name: Al-Anfal
hard.translation: And know that your possessions and your children are a test, and that with Allah is immense reward.

hard.name: Al-Anfal
hard.translation: But Allah would not punish them while thou wast with them, nor will He punish them while they seek forgiveness.

hard.name: Al-Anfal
hard.translation: And if they turn away, then know that Allah is your Befriender - a Transcendent Patron, a Transcendent Helper!

hard.name: Al-Anfal
hard.translation: O ye who believe! When ye meet an army, hold firm and think of Allah much, that ye may be successful.

hard.name: Al-Anfal
hard.translation: This is for that which your own hands have sent before (to the Judgment), and (know) that Allah is not a tyrant to His slaves.

hard.name: Al-Anfal
hard.translation: Lo! the worst of beasts in Allah's sight are the ungrateful who will not believe.

hard.name: Al-Anfal
hard.translation: Those of them with whom thou madest a treaty, and then at every opportunity they break their treaty, and they keep not duty (to Allah).

hard.name: Al-Anfal
hard.translation: If thou comest on them in the war, deal with them so as to strike fear in those who are behind them, that haply they may remember.

hard.name: Al-Anfal
hard.translation: And let not those who disbelieve suppose that they can outstrip (Allah's Purpose). Lo! they cannot escape.

hard.name: Al-Anfal
hard.translation: And if they would deceive thee, then lo! Allah is Sufficient for thee. He it is Who supporteth thee with His help and with the believers,

hard.name: Al-Anfal
hard.translation: Had it not been for an ordinance of Allah which had gone before, an awful doom had come upon you on account of what ye took.

hard.name: Al-Anfal
hard.translation: Now enjoy what ye have won, as lawful and good, and keep your duty to Allah. Lo! Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.

hard.name: At-Tawbah
hard.translation: Freedom from obligation (is proclaimed) from Allah and His messenger toward those of the idolaters with whom ye made a treaty.

hard.name: At-Tawbah
hard.translation: And they observe toward a believer neither pact nor honour. These are they who are transgressors.

hard.name: At-Tawbah
hard.translation: Fight them! Allah will chastise them at your hands, and He will lay them low and give you victory over them, and He will heal the breasts of folk who are believers.

hard.name: At-Tawbah
hard.translation: And He will remove the anger of their hearts. Allah relenteth toward whom He will. Allah is Knower, Wise.

hard.name: At-Tawbah
hard.translation: Their Lord giveth them good tidings of mercy from Him, and acceptance, and Gardens where enduring pleasure will be theirs;

hard.name: At-Tawbah
hard.translation: There they will abide for ever. Lo! with Allah there is immense reward.

hard.name: At-Tawbah
hard.translation: Then afterward Allah will relent toward whom He will; for Allah is Forgiving, Merciful.

hard.name: At-Tawbah
hard.translation: Allah forgive thee (O Muhammad)! Wherefor didst thou grant them leave ere those who told the truth were manifest to thee and thou didst know the liars?

hard.name: At-Tawbah
hard.translation: Say: Pay (your contribution), willingly or unwillingly, it will not be accepted from you. Lo! ye were ever froward folk.

hard.name: At-Tawbah
hard.translation: And they swear by Allah that they are in truth of you, when they are not of you, but they are folk who are afraid.

hard.name: At-Tawbah
hard.translation: Had they but found a refuge, or caverns, or a place to enter, they surely had resorted thither swift as runaways.

hard.name: At-Tawbah
hard.translation: They swear by Allah to you (Muslims) to please you, but Allah, with His messenger, hath more right that they should please Him if they are believers.

hard.name: At-Tawbah
hard.translation: O Prophet! Strive against the disbelievers and the hypocrites! Be harsh with them. Their ultimate abode is hell, a hapless journey's end.

hard.name: At-Tawbah
hard.translation: And of them is he who made a covenant with Allah (saying): If He give us of His bounty we will give alms and become of the righteous.

hard.name: At-Tawbah
hard.translation: Yet when He gave them of His bounty, they hoarded it and turned away, averse;

hard.name: At-Tawbah
hard.translation: Know they not that Allah knoweth both their secret and the thought that they confide, and that Allah is the Knower of Things Hidden?

hard.name: At-Tawbah
hard.translation: They are content that they should be with the useless and their hearts are sealed, so that they apprehend not.

hard.name: At-Tawbah
hard.translation: And (there are) others who await Allah's decree, whether He will punish them or will forgive them. Allah is Knower, Wise.

hard.name: At-Tawbah
hard.translation: But as for those in whose hearts is disease, it only addeth wickedness to their wickedness, and they die while they are disbelievers.

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: Then We appointed you viceroys in the earth after them, that We might see how ye behave.

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: And Allah summoneth to the abode of peace, and leadeth whom He will to a straight path.

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: Allah sufficeth as a witness between us and you, that we were unaware of your worship.

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: Such then is Allah, your rightful Lord. After the Truth what is there saving error? How then are ye turned away!

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: Thus is the Word of thy Lord justified concerning those who do wrong: that they believe not.

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: And of them is he who believeth therein, and of them is he who believeth not therein, and thy Lord is Best Aware of the corrupters.

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: And of them are some who listen unto thee. But canst thou make the deaf to hear even though they apprehend not?

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: And of them is he who looketh toward thee. But canst thou guide the blind even though they see not?

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: Lo! Allah wrongeth not mankind in aught; but mankind wrong themselves.

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: And for every nation there is a messenger. And when their messenger cometh (on the Day of Judgment) it will be judged between them fairly, and they will not be wronged.

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: Say: Have ye thought: When His doom cometh unto you as a raid by night, or in the (busy) day; what is there of it that the guilty ones desire to hasten?

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: Is it (only) then, when it hath befallen you, that ye will believe? What! (Believe) now, when (until now) ye have been hastening it on (through disbelief)?

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: Then will it be said unto those who dealt unjustly Taste the torment of eternity. Are ye requited aught save what ye used to earn?

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: Say: In the bounty of Allah and in His mercy: therein let them rejoice. It is better than what they hoard.

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: Lo! verily the friends of Allah are (those) on whom fear (cometh) not, nor do they grieve?

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: And let not their speech grieve thee (O Muhammad). Lo! power belongeth wholly to Allah. He is the Hearer, the Knower.

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: Say: Verily those who invent a lie concerning Allah will not succeed.

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: This world's portion (will be theirs), then unto Us is their return. Then We make them taste a dreadful doom because they used to disbelieve.

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: And when the Truth from Our presence came unto them, they said: Lo! this is mere magic.

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: Moses said: Speak ye (so) of the Truth when it hath come unto you? Is this magic? Now magicians thrive not.

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: And when the wizards came, Moses said unto them: Cast your cast!

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: And Moses said: O my people! If ye have believed in Allah then put trust in Him, if ye have indeed surrendered (unto Him)!

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: They said: In Allah we put trust. Our Lord! Oh, make us not a lure for the wrongdoing folk;

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: He said: Your prayer is heard. Do ye twain keep to the straight path, and follow not the road of those who have no knowledge.

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: And be not thou of those who deny the revelations of Allah, for then wert thou of the losers.

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: Then shall We save Our messengers and the believers, in like manner (as of old). It is incumbent upon Us to save believers.

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: And, (O Muhammad) set thy purpose resolutely for religion, as a man by nature upright, and be not of those who ascribe partners (to Allah).

hard.name: Yunus
hard.translation: And (O Muhammad) follow that which is inspired in thee, and forbear until Allah give judgment. And He is the Best of Judges.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: Alif. Lam. Ra. (This is) a Scripture the revelations whereof are perfected and then expounded. (It cometh) from One Wise, Informed,

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: (Saying): Serve none but Allah. Lo! I am unto you from Him a warner and a bringer of good tidings.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: Unto Allah is your return, and He is Able to do all things.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: And if we cause man to taste some mercy from Us and afterward withdraw it from him, lo! he is despairing, thankless.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: Save those who persevere and do good works. Theirs will be forgiveness and a great reward.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: Who debar (men) from the way of Allah and would have it crooked, and who are disbelievers in the Hereafter.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: Such are they who have lost their souls, and that which they used to invent hath failed them.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: And We sent Noah unto his folk (and he said): Lo! I am a plain warner unto you.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: That ye serve none, save Allah. Lo! I fear for you the retribution of a painful Day.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: And, O my people! who would deliver me from Allah if I thrust them away? Will ye not then reflect?

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: They said: O Noah! Thou hast disputed with us and multiplied disputation with us; now bring upon us that wherewith thou threatenest us, if thou art of the truthful.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: He said: Only Allah will bring it upon you if He will, and ye can by no means escape.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: Or say they (again): He hath invented it? Say: If I have invented it, upon me be my crimes, but I am innocent of (all) that ye commit.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: Build the ship under Our eyes and by Our inspiration, and speak not unto Me on behalf of those who do wrong. Lo! they will be drowned.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: And ye shall know to whom a punishment that will confound him cometh, and upon whom a lasting doom will fall.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: And he said: Embark therein! In the name of Allah be its course and its mooring. Lo! my Lord is Forgiving, Merciful.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: And such were A'ad. They denied the revelations of their Lord and flouted His messengers and followed the command of every froward potentate.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: But they hamstrung her, and then he said: Enjoy life in your dwelling-place three days! This is a threat that will not be belied.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: And his wife, standing by laughed when We gave her good tidings (of the birth) of Isaac, and, after Isaac, of Jacob.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: She said: Oh woe is me! Shall I bear a child when I am an old woman, and this my husband is an old man? Lo! this is a strange thing!

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: And when the awe departed from Abraham, and the glad news reached him, he pleaded with Us on behalf of the folk of Lot.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: And when Our messengers came unto Lot, he was distressed and knew not how to protect them. He said: This is a distressful day.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: They said: Well thou knowest that we have no right to thy daughters, and well thou knowest what we want.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: He said: Would that I had strength to resist you or had some strong support (among you)!

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: So when Our commandment came to pass We overthrew (that township) and rained upon it stones of clay, one after another,

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: Marked with fire in the providence of thy Lord (for the destruction of the wicked). And they are never far from the wrong-doers.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: That which Allah leaveth with you is better for you if ye are believers; and I am not a keeper over you.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: Ask pardon of your Lord and then turn unto Him (repentant). Lo! my Lord is Merciful, Loving.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: As though they had not dwelt there. A far removal for Midian, even as Thamud had been removed afar!

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: Unto Pharaoh and his chiefs, but they did follow the command of Pharaoh, and the command of Pharaoh was no right guide.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: He will go before his people on the Day of Resurrection and will lead them to the Fire for watering-place. Ah, hapless is the watering-place (whither they are) led.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: A curse is made to follow them in the world and on the Day of Resurrection. Hapless is the gift (that will be) given (them).

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: That is (something) of the tidings of the townships (which were destroyed of old). We relate it unto thee (Muhammad). Some of them are standing and some (already) reaped.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: Even thus is the grasp of thy Lord when He graspeth the townships while they are doing wrong. Lo! His grasp is painful, very strong.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: On the day when it cometh no soul will speak except by His permission; some among them will be wretched, (others) glad.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: As for those who will be wretched (on that day) they will be in the Fire; sighing and wailing will be their portion therein,

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: And lo! unto each thy Lord will verily repay his works in full. Lo! He is Informed of what they do.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: So tread thou the straight path as thou art commanded, and those who turn (unto Allah) with thee, and transgress not. Lo! He is Seer of what ye do.

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: And if thy Lord had willed, He verily would have made mankind one nation, yet they cease not differing,

hard.name: Hud
hard.translation: And say unto those who believe not: Act according to your power. Lo! We (too) are acting.

hard.name: Yusuf
hard.translation: They said: O our father! Why wilt thou not trust us with Joseph, when lo! we are good friends to him?

hard.name: Yusuf
hard.translation: He said: Lo! in truth it saddens me that ye should take him with you, and I fear less the wolf devour him while ye are heedless of him.

hard.name: Yusuf
hard.translation: They said: If the wolf should devour him when we are (so strong) a band, then surely we should have already perished.

hard.name: Yusuf
hard.translation: And they sold him for a low price, a number of silver coins; and they attached no value to him.

hard.name: Yusuf
hard.translation: And And when he reached his prime We gave him wisdom and knowledge. Thus We reward the good.

hard.name: Yusuf
hard.translation: And if his shirt is torn from behind, then she hath lied and he is of the truthful.

hard.name: Yusuf
hard.translation: O Joseph! Turn away from this, and thou, (O woman), ask forgiveness for thy sin. Lo! thou art of the faulty.

hard.name: Yusuf
hard.translation: So his Lord heard his prayer and fended off their wiles from him. Lo! He is Hearer, Knower.

hard.name: Yusuf
hard.translation: And it seemed good to them (the men-folk) after they had seen the signs (of his innocence) to imprison him for a time.

hard.name: Yusuf
hard.translation: O my fellow-prisoners! Are divers lords better, or Allah the One, Almighty?

hard.name: Yusuf
hard.translation: They answered: Jumbled dreams! And we are not knowing in the interpretation of dreams.

hard.name: Yusuf
hard.translation: And he of the two who was released, and (now) at length remembered, said: I am going to announce unto you the interpretation, therefore send me forth.

hard.name: Yusuf
hard.translation: Then, after that, will come a year when the people will have plenteous crops and when they will press (wine and oil).

hard.name: Yusuf
hard.translation: (Then Joseph said: I asked for) this, that he (my lord) may know that I betrayed him not in secret, and that surely Allah guideth not the snare of the betrayers.

hard.name: Yusuf
hard.translation: He said: Set me over the storehouses of the land. Lo! I am a skilled custodian.

hard.name: Yusuf
hard.translation: And Joseph's brethren came and presented themselves before him, and he knew them but they knew him not.

hard.name: Yusuf
hard.translation: And if ye bring him not unto me, then there shall be no measure for you with me, nor shall ye draw near.

hard.name: Yusuf
hard.translation: They said: We have lost the king's cup, and he who bringeth it shall have a camel-load, and I (said Joseph) am answerable for it.

hard.name: Yusuf
hard.translation: They said: By Allah, well ye know we came not to do evil in the land, and are no thieves.

hard.name: Yusuf
hard.translation: They said: The penalty for it! He in whose bag (the cup) is found, he is the penalty for it. Thus we requite wrong-doers.

hard.name: Yusuf
hard.translation: He said: Allah forbid that we should seize save him with whom we found our property; then truly we should be wrong-doers.

hard.name: Yusuf
hard.translation: Ask the township where we were, and the caravan with which we travelled hither. Lo! we speak the truth.

clues: It is one of the five pillars of Islam.
It is obligatory once in a lifetime, for those who are able.
It takes place in and around Makkah.
It happens in the month of Dhul-Hijjah.
It includes Tawaf around the Ka'bah and standing at Arafah.
easy.explain: Hajj is the pilgrimage to Makkah, obligatory once in a lifetime on every Muslim who has the physical and financial means. Umrah shares some rites but can be performed at any time of year and is not one of the pillars.

clues: It is one of the five pillars.
It is performed at set times.
There are five obligatory ones each day.
It is performed facing the qiblah.
It includes ruku' and sujud.
easy.explain: Salah is the five daily obligatory prayers. Du'a and dhikr are forms of worship too, but they are not the specific prescribed prayer, and Tahajjud is a voluntary night prayer.

clues: It is a month of the Islamic calendar.
It is the ninth month.
Fasting in it is obligatory.
The Qur'an began to be revealed in it.
It contains Laylat al-Qadr.
easy.explain: Ramadan is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar and the month of obligatory fasting. Laylat al-Qadr, described as better than a thousand months, falls within its last ten nights.

clues: It is one of the five pillars.
It is obligatory, not voluntary.
It is calculated on wealth held for a lunar year above a threshold.
On most savings it is 2.5%.
The Qur'an names eight categories who may receive it.
easy.explain: Zakat is the obligatory annual charity, commonly 2.5% on qualifying wealth above the nisab threshold. Sadaqah, by contrast, is voluntary and has no fixed amount or time.

clues: It is a building.
It stands in Makkah.
Muslims everywhere face it in prayer.
Its construction is associated with Ibrahim and Isma'il.
Pilgrims walk around it seven times.
easy.explain: The Ka'bah in Makkah is the qiblah, the direction Muslims face in prayer. The Qur'an describes Ibrahim and his son Isma'il raising its foundations.

clues: It is a form of purification.
It is required before the prayer.
It is normally performed with water.
It involves washing the face, arms, and feet.
It includes wiping the head.
easy.explain: Wudu is the ablution required before prayer. Ghusl is the full bath required in certain states, and tayammum is the substitute using clean earth when water is unavailable or harmful.

clues: It is one of the five pillars.
It is obligatory for one month each year.
It is observed during daylight hours.
It involves abstaining from food and drink.
It begins at dawn and ends at sunset.
easy.explain: Sawm is the obligatory fast of Ramadan, kept from the break of dawn until sunset. It involves abstaining from food, drink and marital relations during those hours.

clues: It is the first of the five pillars.
It is a statement, not an action.
It has two parts.
Saying it sincerely is how a person enters Islam.
It affirms that there is no god but Allah and that Muhammad is His Messenger.
easy.explain: The shahada is the testimony of faith and the first pillar. Its two parts affirm the oneness of Allah and the messengership of Muhammad ﷺ.

clues: It is a revealed book.
It was revealed in Arabic.
It was revealed in stages over about twenty-three years.
It contains 114 chapters.
It was revealed to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
easy.explain: The Qur'an was revealed to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ over approximately twenty-three years, and consists of 114 surahs.

clues: It is a day of celebration.
It involves a special congregational prayer.
It marks the end of something.
That something is a month of fasting.
It falls on the first of Shawwal.
easy.explain: Eid al-Fitr falls on 1 Shawwal and marks the end of Ramadan. Zakat al-Fitr is given before the Eid prayer.

clues: It is a day of celebration.
It falls in Dhul-Hijjah.
It comes during the days of Hajj.
It commemorates the willingness of Ibrahim to sacrifice his son.
An animal is sacrificed and its meat shared.
easy.explain: Eid al-Adha falls on 10 Dhul-Hijjah, during the Hajj. It commemorates Ibrahim's willingness to sacrifice his son, and the meat of the sacrifice is traditionally shared in thirds.

clues: It is spoken aloud.
It is called out from a mosque.
It happens five times a day.
It begins with Allahu akbar, repeated.
It is the call to prayer.
easy.explain: The adhan is the call to prayer, announced before each of the five obligatory prayers. The iqamah is the shorter second call given immediately before the prayer begins.

clues: It is a congregational prayer.
It happens once a week.
It takes place on Friday.
It replaces the Dhuhr prayer that day.
It is preceded by a sermon.
easy.explain: Jumu'ah is the Friday congregational prayer, preceded by a khutbah (sermon). It takes the place of Dhuhr on that day for those obliged to attend.

clues: It is a rite performed in Makkah.
It is performed inside the Masjid al-Haram.
It involves movement, not standing still.
It is done seven times.
It is performed around the Ka'bah.
easy.explain: Tawaf is circling the Ka'bah seven times, performed during both Hajj and Umrah. Sa'i, by contrast, is the walking between Safa and Marwah.

clues: It is a journey of worship to Makkah.
It is not one of the five pillars.
It can be performed at any time of year.
It is shorter than the greater pilgrimage.
It consists mainly of Tawaf and Sa'i.
easy.explain: Umrah is the lesser pilgrimage. Unlike Hajj it is not one of the five pillars and has no fixed season, and it consists principally of ihram, Tawaf and Sa'i.

clues: He is an angel.
He is named in the Qur'an.
He carried out a particular duty for Allah.
That duty was bringing revelation.
He brought the first revelation at the cave of Hira.
easy.explain: Jibril (Gabriel) is the angel charged with bringing revelation to the prophets. He brought the first verses of Surah Al-Alaq to the Prophet ﷺ at the cave of Hira.

clues: It is a city.
It is in the Arabian peninsula.
It was formerly known by another name, Yathrib.
The Prophet ﷺ migrated to it.
He is buried there.
easy.explain: Madinah, formerly called Yathrib, is the city the Prophet ﷺ migrated to in 622 CE. His mosque and resting place are there.

clues: It is a short phrase.
It is said before beginning many things.
It opens almost every surah of the Qur'an.
One surah, At-Tawbah, does not begin with it.
It means: In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
easy.explain: The Basmalah opens 113 of the 114 surahs; Surah At-Tawbah is the exception. Scholars differ over whether it is counted as an ayah of Al-Fatihah.

clues: It is a position within the prayer.
It is performed twice in each unit.
It is the lowest position of the prayer.
Seven parts of the body touch the ground.
The forehead rests on the ground.
easy.explain: Sujud is prostration, performed twice in each rak'ah. It is described as the position in which a servant is closest to their Lord.

clues: It is connected with fasting.
It happens while it is still dark.
It takes place before the fast begins.
It ends at the break of dawn.
It is the pre-dawn meal.
easy.explain: Suhur is the meal eaten before dawn when fasting. Iftar is the meal that breaks the fast at sunset.

clues: It is a city.
It is the birthplace of the Prophet ﷺ.
It contains the Masjid al-Haram.
Muslims face it in prayer.
The Ka'bah stands at its centre.
easy.explain: Makkah is the city of the Ka'bah and the birthplace of the Prophet ﷺ. It is the destination of Hajj and the direction of prayer for Muslims worldwide.

clues: He was a prophet.
He called his people for a very long time.
Few of them believed him.
He was commanded to build something large.
He built an ark before the flood.
easy.explain: Nuh (Noah), ʿalayhi al-salām, called his people for many years before being commanded to build the ark. Surah Nuh is named after him.

clues: He was a prophet.
He was raised in a royal household that was not his own.
He was sent to a tyrant king.
He was given a scripture, the Tawrat.
His staff became a serpent, and the sea parted for him.
easy.explain: Musa (Moses), ʿalayhi al-salām, is the prophet most often named in the Qur'an. He was sent to Pharaoh and given the Tawrat.

clues: He was a prophet.
He had a dream as a child involving stars.
His brothers threw him into a well.
He later interpreted the dreams of a king.
A surah of the Qur'an is named after him and tells his story.
easy.explain: Surah Yusuf tells the story of Yusuf (Joseph), ʿalayhi al-salām, in one continuous narrative — unusual in the Qur'an.

clues: He was a prophet.
He is called a friend of Allah, Khalilullah.
He argued against the idols of his people.
He was thrown into a fire that was made cool for him.
He and his son raised the foundations of the Ka'bah.
easy.explain: Ibrahim (Abraham), ʿalayhi al-salām, is one of the five Ulul-Azm prophets. With his son Isma'il he raised the foundations of the Ka'bah.

clues: She is a woman mentioned in the Qur'an.
She is the only woman named in the Qur'an by her own name.
A surah is named after her.
She is described as chosen above the women of the worlds.
She is the mother of Prophet Isa.
easy.explain: Maryam is the only woman named by name in the Qur'an, and Surah Maryam (19) is named after her. She is the mother of Prophet Isa, ʿalayhi al-salām.

clues: It is a place in the hereafter.
It is the reward promised to the believers.
It is described as containing rivers.
It is entered after the Day of Judgement.
It is the garden, or paradise.
easy.explain: Jannah is paradise, the reward of the believers, described throughout the Qur'an as gardens beneath which rivers flow.

clues: It is the most central concept in Islam.
It concerns Allah alone.
It is the opposite of shirk.
Surah Al-Ikhlas is entirely about it.
It means the absolute oneness of Allah.
easy.explain: Tawhid is the affirmation of the absolute oneness of Allah, the foundation of Islamic belief and the opposite of shirk, associating partners with Him.

clues: It is a source of guidance in Islam.
It is not the Qur'an itself.
It concerns one particular person.
It refers to his sayings, actions and approvals.
It is the way of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
easy.explain: The Sunnah is the practice of the Prophet ﷺ — his sayings, actions and tacit approvals. Hadith are the reports through which the Sunnah is transmitted.

clues: It is a unit of something.
It belongs to the prayer.
Each one contains standing, bowing and prostrating.
Fajr has two of them.
Dhuhr has four of them.
easy.explain: A rak'ah is one complete unit of prayer. Fajr has two, Maghrib three, and Dhuhr, Asr and Isha four each.

clues: It is connected with fasting.
It happens at a precise moment each day.
It is traditionally begun with dates and water.
It takes place when the sun sets.
It is the meal that breaks the fast.
easy.explain: Iftar is the breaking of the fast at sunset, traditionally with dates and water, followed by the Maghrib prayer.

clues: It is a mosque.
It is in Madinah.
It was established by the Prophet ﷺ after the Hijrah.
It is the second holiest mosque in Islam.
The Prophet ﷺ is buried within it.
easy.explain: Masjid an-Nabawi, the Prophet's Mosque in Madinah, was established after the Hijrah and is the second holiest mosque in Islam.

clues: It is a form of giving.
It is encouraged but not compulsory.
It has no fixed rate.
It can be given at any time, in any amount.
Even a smile is described as a form of it.
easy.explain: Sadaqah is voluntary charity, with no fixed amount or time. Zakat, by contrast, is the obligatory annual charity with defined rules.

clues: It is a division of the Qur'an.
It is larger than a single verse.
Each one has a name.
There are 114 of them.
The first is Al-Fatihah and the last is An-Nas.
easy.explain: A surah is a chapter of the Qur'an. There are 114, ranging from three ayahs (Al-Kawthar) to 286 (Al-Baqarah).

clues: It is a division of the Qur'an.
It is smaller than a chapter.
The word also means a sign.
They are numbered within each chapter.
There are over six thousand of them in total.
easy.explain: An ayah is a verse of the Qur'an; the word also means 'sign'. The commonly cited total is 6,236 in the Hafs reading.

clues: It is an event yet to come.
Belief in it is one of the articles of faith.
It follows the end of this world.
People will be raised and gathered.
Deeds will be weighed and recompensed.
easy.explain: Yawm al-Qiyamah, the Day of Judgement, is one of the six articles of faith. The dead are resurrected, gathered, and recompensed for their deeds.

clues: It is an act of worship.
It can be done at any time, anywhere.
It needs no fixed posture.
It involves repeating certain phrases.
It is the remembrance of Allah.
easy.explain: Dhikr is the remembrance of Allah through phrases such as SubhanAllah, Alhamdulillah and Allahu akbar. It requires no fixed time or posture.

clues: It is an act of worship.
It can be made in any language.
It is personal rather than fixed in form.
It is described as the essence of worship.
It is calling upon Allah and asking of Him.
