The Qur'an warns that enmity to him is enmity to Allah.
His name is often written Michael in English.
easy.explain: Mika'il is one of the two angels named in Surah Al-Baqarah, alongside Jibril. The Prophet ﷺ also mentioned him in his night prayer supplication.

clues: It is a mosque.
It is the largest mosque in the world.
Prayer in it is worth more than prayer anywhere else.
Muslims everywhere face it in prayer.
The Ka'bah stands in its centre.
easy.explain: Masjid al-Haram in Makkah surrounds the Ka'bah. The Qur'an commands the believers to turn their faces towards it in prayer.

clues: It is a valley near Makkah.
Pilgrims stay there during Hajj.
It is known as a city of tents.
The pillars of the Jamarat are there.
Pilgrims spend the days of Tashriq there.
easy.explain: Mina lies between Makkah and Muzdalifah. Pilgrims go there on the 8th of Dhul-Hijjah and return after Arafah to stone the Jamarat.

clues: It lies on the route of the Hajj.
Pilgrims arrive there after sunset on the day of Arafah.
They pray Maghrib and Isha there together.
Many pick up their pebbles for stoning there.
The Qur'an calls a place there the Sacred Monument.
easy.explain: Pilgrims leave Arafah after sunset and spend the night at Muzdalifah. The Qur'an tells them to remember Allah at the Sacred Monument (al-Mash'ar al-Haram).

clues: They are two small hills.
They are now inside the Masjid al-Haram.
Hajar ran between them looking for water.
Pilgrims walk between them seven times.
The Qur'an calls them among the signs of Allah.
easy.explain: Sa'i is the walk between Safa and Marwah. The Qur'an says they are among the symbols of Allah.

clues: It is a small cave on a mountain near Makkah.
The Prophet ﷺ used to go there to worship alone.
He would take food with him for several nights.
Jibril came to him there.
The first verses of the Qur'an were revealed there.
easy.explain: Before prophethood, the Prophet ﷺ would retreat to the cave of Hira. There Jibril came with the first verses: "Read in the name of your Lord."

clues: It is on a mountain south of Makkah.
Two men hid there for three nights.
The Quraysh searched for them right up to its mouth.
One of the men said, "Do not grieve, Allah is with us."
The Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr hid there during the Hijrah.
easy.explain: During the Hijrah the Prophet ﷺ and Abu Bakr hid in the cave of Thawr. The Qur'an recalls the moment he said, "Grieve not, Allah is with us."

clues: It is a mountain.
It lies just north of Madinah.
A major battle was fought at its foot.
Hamzah is buried near it.
The Prophet ﷺ said it loves us and we love it.
easy.explain: Mount Uhud overlooks Madinah. The Prophet ﷺ said, "This is a mountain that loves us and we love it."

clues: It is a cemetery.
It is in Madinah, next to Masjid an-Nabawi.
Many companions are buried there.
The Prophet ﷺ would go out at night to pray for those buried there.
Its full name is Baqi' al-Gharqad.
easy.explain: Al-Baqi' is the main cemetery of Madinah. The Prophet ﷺ visited it and prayed for its people.

clues: It is a land across the Red Sea from Arabia.
Its king was known for his justice.
Muslims fled there to escape persecution in Makkah.
Ja'far ibn Abi Talib spoke before its king.
Its king was the Negus, al-Najashi.
easy.explain: Muslims migrated to Abyssinia twice during the Makkan period. When the Negus died, the Prophet ﷺ led the funeral prayer for him in his absence.

clues: It is a prayer.
It is prayed after Isha.
It is prayed in an odd number of rak'ahs.
Many make it the last prayer of the night.
Its name means "odd".
easy.explain: Witr is prayed after Isha and before Fajr in an odd number of rak'ahs. The Prophet ﷺ said, "Make witr the last of your prayers at night."

clues: It is a voluntary prayer.
It is prayed in daytime.
Its time begins after the sun has risen well above the horizon.
Abu Hurayrah said the Prophet ﷺ advised him to pray two rak'ahs of it.
It is named after the forenoon.
easy.explain: Abu Hurayrah said his friend ﷺ advised him to fast three days each month, pray two rak'ahs of Duha, and pray witr before sleeping.

clues: It is a congregational prayer.
It has no ruku' and no sujud.
It is prayed standing with four takbirs.
Attending it earns a reward like a mountain.
It is prayed for a Muslim who has died.
easy.explain: The funeral prayer is offered for the deceased. The Prophet ﷺ said whoever attends it until the prayer is offered gets one qirat of reward, and a qirat is like a mountain.

clues: It is a call.
It is said just before the obligatory prayer begins.
Its words are close to those of the adhan.
It includes the phrase "the prayer has begun".
Bilal was told to say its phrases once and the adhan's twice.
easy.explain: The iqamah is the second call, given when the prayer is about to start. Bilal was ordered to say the adhan phrases twice and the iqamah phrases once.

clues: It is recited in the prayer.
It is said while sitting.
It begins with greetings to Allah.
It includes the testimony of faith.
Ibn Mas'ud said the Prophet ﷺ taught it to him as he would teach a surah.
easy.explain: The tashahhud is recited in the sitting of the prayer. It begins "At-tahiyyatu lillah" and ends with the testimony of faith.

clues: It is needed for every act of worship.
It is in the heart, not on the tongue.
It turns a habit into worship.
The first hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari is about it.
The word means "intention".
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said, "Actions are judged by intentions, and every person will have what they intended."

clues: It is made from the twig of a tree.
It is used every day.
It cleans the mouth.
The Prophet ﷺ would have ordered it before every prayer if it were not hard on people.
Its other name is siwak.
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said, "If it were not hard on my followers, I would have ordered them to use the siwak before every prayer."

clues: It is a phrase repeated often.
It is said aloud by men.
It is said by people in ihram.
It is said until the stoning on the day of Eid.
It begins "Labbayk Allahumma labbayk".
easy.explain: Pilgrims in ihram repeat the talbiyah: "Here I am, O Allah, here I am. You have no partner, here I am."

clues: It is an act of worship done once a year.
It involves an animal.
Its time begins after the Eid prayer.
The Prophet ﷺ offered two rams.
It is the sacrifice of Eid al-Adha.
easy.explain: Udhiyah is the sacrifice offered on Eid al-Adha and the days after it. Anas reported that the Prophet ﷺ sacrificed two rams.

clues: It is connected to a happy occasion.
It involves sacrificing an animal.
It is done for a child.
It is traditionally done on the seventh day.
The Prophet ﷺ said, "With the boy there is an aqiqah."
easy.explain: Aqiqah is the sacrifice for a newborn. The Prophet ﷺ said, "With the boy there is an aqiqah, so slaughter for him."

clues: It is a meal.
It is sunnah to hold one.
Guests who are invited should accept.
The Prophet ﷺ said, "even if only with one sheep".
It is the wedding feast.
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ told Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf after his marriage, "Give a wedding banquet, even if only with one sheep."

clues: It is a kind of charity.
Its reward keeps coming.
It continues after a person dies.
Building a well or a mosque can be an example.
Its name means "flowing charity".
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said that when a person dies their deeds end except for three: an ongoing charity, beneficial knowledge, or a righteous child who prays for them.

clues: It is a day of the year.
Fasting it is sunnah.
It falls in Muharram.
Musa and his people were saved on it.
It is the 10th of Muharram.
easy.explain: When the Prophet ﷺ came to Madinah he found the Jews fasting Ashura because Allah saved Musa on that day. He said, "We are closer to Musa than you," and fasted it.

clues: It is a month.
It is one of the four sacred months.
Ashura falls in it.
The Prophet ﷺ called it "the month of Allah".
It is the first month of the Islamic year.
easy.explain: Muharram opens the Hijri year. The Prophet ﷺ said the best fasting after Ramadan is in Allah's month of Muharram.

clues: It is a month.
It comes just before a very important month.
The Prophet ﷺ fasted more in it than in any month other than Ramadan.
It is the eighth month of the Islamic year.
Ramadan comes straight after it.
easy.explain: Aishah said she never saw the Prophet ﷺ fast a whole month except Ramadan, and never saw him fast more in any month than in Sha'ban.

clues: He is an angel.
Every living soul will meet him.
He has helpers among the angels.
He takes souls at the appointed time.
The Qur'an calls him the angel of death who is given charge of you.
easy.explain: Surah As-Sajdah says the angel of death, who has been given charge of you, will take your souls, then you will be returned to your Lord.

clues: They are two angels.
They come after burial.
They question a person in the grave.
They ask about his Lord, his religion and his prophet.
Their names are mentioned in a hadith in Jami' al-Tirmidhi.
easy.explain: A hadith in al-Tirmidhi (graded hasan) names the two angels of the grave as Munkar and Nakir.

clues: It is part of the Day of Judgement.
Everyone will have to cross it.
Some cross it like lightning, others crawl.
It is set over Hell.
It is a bridge.
easy.explain: The Sirat is the bridge laid over Hell on the Day of Judgement, described in the long hadith of Abu Hurayrah in Sahih al-Bukhari.

clues: It is part of the Day of Judgement.
Nothing will be wronged on it, even a mustard seed.
Good and bad deeds are placed on it.
Heavy good deeds mean success.
It is the scale.
easy.explain: Allah says He will set up just scales on the Day of Resurrection, and no soul will be wronged in the least, even if it is the weight of a mustard seed.

clues: It is a stage everyone will pass through.
It begins at death.
It lasts until the Resurrection.
Those in it cannot return to this world.
Its name means "barrier".
easy.explain: Surah Al-Mu'minun says that behind those who die is a barrier (barzakh) until the day they are raised.

clues: They are a creation of Allah.
Most people cannot see them.
Some of them are believers and some are not.
They were created from smokeless fire.
A whole surah is named after them.
easy.explain: The jinn were created from smokeless fire. Surah Al-Jinn tells of a group of them who heard the Qur'an and believed.

clues: It is in Makkah.
It is set in a corner of a building.
Pilgrims try to kiss it or point to it.
Umar said, "I know you are only a stone."
It is in the eastern corner of the Ka'bah.
easy.explain: The Black Stone is set in the eastern corner of the Ka'bah, where tawaf begins. Umar kissed it, saying he did so only because he had seen the Prophet ﷺ kiss it.

clues: It is inside the Masjid al-Haram.
It is a stone.
It is linked to the building of the Ka'bah.
Pilgrims pray two rak'ahs behind it after tawaf.
The Qur'an calls it the place where Ibrahim stood.
easy.explain: Allah says, "Take as your place of prayer the place where Ibrahim stood." After tawaf, pilgrims pray two rak'ahs behind it.

clues: It was made of wood.
Its builder's people mocked him each time they passed by.
People mocked its builder.
It carried pairs of every kind of animal.
It came to rest on Mount Judi.
easy.explain: Nuh built the ship by Allah's command while his people mocked him. After the flood it came to rest on al-Judi.

clues: It belonged to a prophet.
He leaned on it and used it to herd his sheep.
It turned into a snake.
It split the sea.
Water gushed from a rock when it was struck with it.
easy.explain: Musa said of his staff, "I lean on it and beat down leaves for my sheep." By Allah's leave it became a serpent, parted the sea and brought water from the rock.

clues: It is an animal mentioned in the Qur'an.
It was a sign for a people.
It was given its own day to drink.
Its people were told not to harm it, but they killed it.
It was sent to the people of Thamud.
easy.explain: Salih told Thamud, "This is the camel of Allah, a sign for you, so leave her to graze." They hamstrung her and were destroyed.

options: The fish of Musa and Khidr
clues: It is a creature from the stories of the prophets.
It lived in the sea.
It swallowed a man.
The man inside it prayed in the darkness.
The prophet it swallowed is called Dhun-Nun.
easy.explain: Yunus was swallowed by the fish and called out in the darkness, "There is no god but You, glory be to You." Allah saved him.

clues: It is a bird.
It was missing when a king inspected his birds.
It returned with news from a faraway land.
It told of a queen and her people who worshipped the sun.
It served Prophet Sulayman.
easy.explain: Sulayman noticed the hoopoe was absent. It came back with news of the people of Saba' and their queen.

clues: It is a tiny creature.
It spoke to others of its kind.
It warned them of an army coming.
Its words made a prophet smile.
A surah is named after its kind.
easy.explain: An ant told the others to enter their dwellings so that Sulayman and his armies would not crush them unknowingly. Sulayman smiled at its words.

clues: They were sent against an army.
They came in flocks.
They threw stones of baked clay.
The army had come to destroy the Ka'bah.
Their story is told in Surah Al-Fil.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Fil tells how Allah sent flocks of birds against the army of the elephant, pelting them with stones of baked clay.

clues: It is an animal from a story in the Qur'an.
A people were told to slaughter it.
They kept asking questions about it.
Part of it was used to reveal a murderer.
The longest surah is named after it.
easy.explain: Musa told his people that Allah commanded them to slaughter a cow. They kept asking about its age and colour. Surah Al-Baqarah is named after it.

clues: It is an animal mentioned in the Qur'an.
It lay with its forelegs stretched out.
It guarded the entrance of a shelter.
It slept for many years with a group of young men.
It belonged to the People of the Cave.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Kahf describes the sleepers in the cave, with their dog stretching its forelegs at the entrance.

clues: It was an idol.
It was made from melted jewellery.
It made a lowing sound.
It was made while Musa was away.
It was made by al-Samiri.
easy.explain: While Musa was away, al-Samiri made a calf from the people's ornaments and many worshipped it. Musa burned it and scattered its remains in the sea.

clues: It is a revealed scripture.
The Qur'an says it contained guidance and light.
Its laws were judged by prophets after its messenger.
It was revealed to Bani Isra'il.
It was given to Musa.
easy.explain: Allah says, "We revealed the Torah, in which was guidance and light." It was given to Musa.

clues: It is a revealed scripture.
It confirmed the scripture before it.
The Qur'an says it contained guidance and light.
It was revealed after the Tawrat.
It was given to Isa.
easy.explain: Allah says He gave Isa son of Maryam the Gospel, containing guidance and light, confirming the Torah before it.

clues: It is a revealed scripture.
It is named in the Qur'an.
Its prophet was also a king.
Mountains and birds glorified Allah with its prophet.
It was given to Dawud.
easy.explain: Allah says, "And to Dawud We gave the Psalms (Zabur)."

clues: It is a place in the Hereafter.
It is a reward for those who believe and do good.
The Prophet ﷺ told us to ask Allah for it.
Above it is the Throne of the Most Merciful.
It is the highest level of Paradise.
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said, "When you ask Allah, ask Him for al-Firdaws, for it is the middle and highest part of Paradise."

clues: It is in Paradise.
It is a gate.
Only one group of people will enter through it.
It is closed after they have entered.
It is for those who fasted.
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said there is a gate in Paradise called ar-Rayyan, through which only those who fasted will enter.

clues: He will appear before the end of time.
He will be a great trial for people.
He will claim to be a lord.
He is blind in one eye.
Isa son of Maryam will kill him.
easy.explain: The long hadith of al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an in Sahih Muslim describes the Dajjal's trial and his killing by Isa ibn Maryam.

clues: They are two peoples.
They spread corruption in the land.
A wall was built to hold them back.
Dhul-Qarnayn built that wall.
They will pour out from every height near the end of time.
easy.explain: Dhul-Qarnayn built a barrier of iron and copper against Ya'juj and Ma'juj (Gog and Magog). Near the Hour they will be let loose.

clues: It belongs to the events of the Last Day.
An angel will blow it.
At the first blow everyone will fall dead.
At the second blow everyone will rise.
In Arabic it is called al-Sur.
easy.explain: Allah says the Trumpet will be blown and all in the heavens and earth will fall dead, then it will be blown again and they will stand looking on.

clues: It is a voluntary fast.
It comes after an obligatory fast.
It is sunnah, not obligatory.
Together with Ramadan it is like fasting the whole year.
It is done in the month after Ramadan.
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said, "Whoever fasts Ramadan and follows it with six days of Shawwal, it is as if he fasted for a lifetime."

clues: It is a voluntary fast.
It comes round every week.
The Prophet ﷺ was asked about it.
He said it was the day he was born.
He also said it was the day revelation first came to him.
easy.explain: Asked about fasting on Monday, the Prophet ﷺ said, "That is the day on which I was born and on which revelation came to me."

clues: It is a voluntary prayer.
It is two rak'ahs.
It is linked to a place.
It is prayed before sitting down.
Its name means "greeting the mosque".
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said, "When one of you enters the mosque, let him pray two rak'ahs before sitting."

clues: It is a sunnah prayer.
It is short.
The Prophet ﷺ never left it, even when travelling.
He said it is better than the world and all it contains.
It is prayed just before the dawn prayer.
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said, "The two rak'ahs of Fajr are better than the world and all that is in it."

clues: It is a month.
It is one of the four sacred months.
It is the only sacred month that stands on its own.
It comes between Jumada al-Akhirah and Sha'ban.
It is the seventh month of the Islamic year.
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ named the four sacred months: three in a row, Dhul-Qa'dah, Dhul-Hijjah and Muharram, and Rajab, which falls between Jumada and Sha'ban.

clues: It is a month.
It is one of the four sacred months.
Its first ten days are the best days of the year.
Eid al-Adha falls in it.
Hajj takes place in it.
easy.explain: Dhul-Hijjah is the twelfth month, the month of Hajj and Eid al-Adha. The Prophet ﷺ said no good deeds are better than those done in its first ten days.

clues: It is a month.
It starts with a celebration.
Fasting six days of it is recommended.
The Battle of Uhud took place in it.
It is the month after Ramadan.
easy.explain: Shawwal begins with Eid al-Fitr. The Prophet ﷺ encouraged fasting six of its days.

clues: It is said many times a day.
It is a duty to answer it.
Adam was told to greet the angels with it.
The Prophet ﷺ said spreading it brings love between people.
It means "peace be upon you".
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said, "Shall I not tell you of something which, if you do it, you will love one another? Spread the salam among you."

clues: It is a short phrase of remembrance.
It is the first phrase after the basmalah in Al-Fatihah.
It is said after sneezing.
The Prophet ﷺ said it fills the scale.
It means "all praise is for Allah".
easy.explain: Al-Fatihah opens with it, and the Prophet ﷺ said, "Alhamdulillah fills the scale."

clues: It is a short phrase.
It is said about the future.
The Qur'an teaches it in Surah Al-Kahf.
It is said when someone plans to do something tomorrow.
It means "if Allah wills".
easy.explain: Allah says, "Never say of anything, I shall do that tomorrow, except (with the words) if Allah wills."

clues: It is a form of remembrance.
Allah and His angels do it.
The believers are commanded to do it.
It is recited in the final sitting of the prayer.
It means sending blessings on the Prophet ﷺ.
easy.explain: Allah says, "Allah and His angels send blessings on the Prophet. O you who believe, send blessings on him and greet him with peace."

clues: It is a short phrase.
It is a request for protection.
It is said against Shaytan.
It is said before reciting the Qur'an.
It is "A'udhu billahi min ash-shaytan ir-rajim".
easy.explain: Allah says, "When you recite the Qur'an, seek refuge in Allah from Satan the outcast."

clues: It is a congregational prayer.
It has no adhan and no iqamah.
It is prayed in the morning, often in an open space.
It has extra takbirs and is followed by a sermon.
It is prayed twice a year.
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ would go out to the musalla on Eid al-Fitr and Eid al-Adha. The first thing he did was pray, then he gave the sermon.

clues: It is a position in the prayer.
It comes after the recitation while standing.
The back is kept straight in it.
"Subhana Rabbiyal Adhim" is said in it.
It is bowing.
easy.explain: Allah says, "O you who believe, bow down and prostrate." In ruku' the worshipper bows with a straight back and glorifies the Lord, the Most Great.

clues: It is a speech.
It is given standing on the minbar.
Talking during it, even to say "be quiet", is forbidden.
It is given twice, with a short sitting in between.
It is the Friday sermon.
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said that if you tell your companion to be quiet on Friday while the imam is giving the khutbah, you have spoken idly.

clues: It is a contract.
It needs offer and acceptance.
It is witnessed.
The Prophet ﷺ said to choose a partner for their religion.
It is the Islamic marriage.
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said a woman is married for four things, her wealth, lineage, beauty and religion, and told us to choose the one with religion.

clues: It is a covering.
It is worn by Muslim women.
Surah An-Nur commands it.
Women are told to draw it over their chests.
In Arabic its root means "to screen".
easy.explain: Surah An-Nur tells believing women to draw their head coverings over their chests, and Surah Al-Ahzab mentions their outer garments.

clues: It is a town in the mountains near Makkah.
It is cooler than Makkah and known for its fruit.
The Prophet ﷺ went there to invite its people to Islam.
Its people drove him out, throwing stones.
The Muslims besieged it after Hunayn.
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ travelled to Ta'if, the town of Thaqif, and was driven out. After Hunayn the Muslims besieged it.

clues: It is a city.
Many prophets lived there.
The Muslims first prayed facing it.
The Prophet ﷺ was taken there on the Night Journey.
Masjid al-Aqsa is there.
easy.explain: The Muslims prayed towards Bayt al-Maqdis for about sixteen or seventeen months after the Hijrah. The Night Journey took the Prophet ﷺ to its mosque.

clues: It is an obligatory prayer.
It has two rak'ahs.
Its recitation is said aloud.
"Prayer is better than sleep" is added to its adhan.
It is prayed at dawn.
easy.explain: The Qur'an speaks of the recitation at dawn, which is witnessed. Its time runs from true dawn until sunrise.

clues: It is an obligatory prayer.
It has four rak'ahs.
Its recitation is silent.
On Friday Jumu'ah replaces it.
Its time starts when the sun passes its highest point.
easy.explain: Dhuhr begins once the sun has passed its highest point. The Prophet ﷺ said, "When you pray Zuhr, its time is until 'Asr comes."

clues: It is an obligatory prayer.
It has four rak'ahs.
Its recitation is silent.
Many scholars say it is the "middle prayer".
It is prayed in the afternoon.
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said the time of Asr lasts until the sun turns yellow. Many scholars identify it with the middle prayer the Qur'an tells us to guard.

clues: It is an obligatory prayer.
It is the only one with three rak'ahs.
People who are fasting break their fast at its time.
Its time ends when the red twilight disappears.
It is prayed at sunset.
easy.explain: Maghrib is prayed after sunset, and its time lasts until the twilight has gone.

clues: It is an obligatory prayer.
It has four rak'ahs.
The first two are recited aloud.
Witr is prayed after it.
It is the last obligatory prayer of the day.
easy.explain: Isha is the night prayer. The Prophet ﷺ said its time lasts to the middle of the night.

clues: It is a role in congregational prayer.
Everyone else follows this person.
No one may move before this person does.
The one who knows the most Qur'an should be chosen for it.
This person leads the prayer.
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said, "The imam is appointed to be followed, so do not differ from him."

clues: It is a mountain.
Allah swears by it in the Qur'an.
A prophet was called from beside it.
Allah spoke to Musa there.
In Arabic it is often called at-Tur.
easy.explain: Allah swears "by Mount Sinai" in Surah At-Tin, and tells how He called Musa from the right side of the Mount.

clues: It is a pair of prostrations.
It is not done in every prayer.
It is done near the end of the prayer.
It makes up for something.
It is the prostration for forgetfulness.
easy.explain: When the Prophet ﷺ forgot part of a prayer he made two prostrations to make up for it, known as the prostrations of forgetfulness.

clues: It is a congregational prayer.
It is prayed in a time of hardship.
The Prophet ﷺ turned his cloak inside out in it.
It is prayed in an open place.
It is the prayer asking for rain.
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ went out to pray for rain, faced the qiblah and turned his cloak around.

clues: It is a congregational prayer.
Each rak'ah has two bowings.
It was prayed on the day the Prophet's son Ibrahim died.
The Prophet ﷺ said these signs do not happen for anyone's death.
It is prayed during an eclipse.
easy.explain: On the day Ibrahim died there was an eclipse. The Prophet ﷺ said the sun and moon are two signs of Allah that do not eclipse for anyone's death, and he led the prayer.

clues: It is in Madinah.
It is inside Masjid an-Nabawi.
It lies between two places connected to the Prophet ﷺ.
Its carpet is a different colour from the rest of the mosque.
The Prophet ﷺ called it a garden from the gardens of Paradise.
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ said, "Between my house and my pulpit is a garden from the gardens of Paradise."

clues: He was a prophet.
He was very old and his wife was barren.
He prayed quietly for a son.
He took care of Maryam in the sanctuary.
His son was Yahya.
easy.explain: Zakariyya called on his Lord in secret for an heir, and Allah gave him the good news of Yahya. He was also Maryam's guardian.

clues: He was a prophet.
He was given wisdom while still a child.
No one before him had been given his name.
He was kind to his parents and never arrogant.
He was the son of Zakariyya.
easy.explain: Allah gave Zakariyya the good news of a son "whose name is Yahya; We have given that name to none before him."

clues: He was a prophet sent to an Arab people.
His people carved homes out of the mountains.
They asked him for a miracle.
They killed the she-camel sent to them.
He was sent to Thamud.
easy.explain: Salih was sent to Thamud, who hewed houses in the mountains. They killed the she-camel of Allah and a mighty blast seized them.

clues: He was a prophet sent to an Arab people.
His people were tall and strong and built lofty buildings.
They boasted, "Who is mightier than us?"
They were destroyed by a furious wind.
He was sent to 'Ad.
easy.explain: Hud was sent to 'Ad, his brother in kinship. They rejected him and were destroyed by a roaring wind for seven nights and eight days.

clues: It is a single night.
It falls within Ramadan.
It is sought in the last ten nights.
It is most often sought on the odd nights.
The Qur'an calls it better than a thousand months.
medium.explain: Laylat al-Qadr, the Night of Decree, is described in Surah Al-Qadr as better than a thousand months. It is sought in the last ten nights of Ramadan, most commonly on the odd-numbered ones; its exact night is not fixed in the sources.

clues: It was a journey.
It involved leaving one city for another.
It went from Makkah to Madinah.
It took place in 622 CE.
The Islamic calendar counts its years from it.
medium.explain: The Hijrah was the migration of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ and his companions from Makkah to Madinah in 622 CE. The Islamic (Hijri) calendar takes its starting point from that year.

clues: It is a source of water.
It is in Makkah.
It is close to the Ka'bah.
Its origin is associated with Hajar searching for water.
Pilgrims drink from it during Hajj and Umrah.
medium.explain: Zamzam is the well within the Masjid al-Haram in Makkah. Its origin is traditionally connected to Hajar searching for water for her infant son Isma'il between Safa and Marwah.

clues: It is a voluntary act of worship.
It is strongly associated with Ramadan.
It involves staying in one place.
That place is the mosque.
It is most commonly observed in the last ten days.
medium.explain: I'tikaf is a period of seclusion in the mosque devoted to worship, most commonly observed during the last ten days of Ramadan, following the practice of the Prophet ﷺ.

clues: It is a single day.
It falls in Dhul-Hijjah.
It is the ninth of that month.
Pilgrims gather on a plain outside Makkah.
Standing there is an essential pillar of Hajj.
medium.explain: The Day of Arafah is 9 Dhul-Hijjah. The standing (wuquf) at Arafah is an essential pillar of Hajj — a pilgrim who misses it has missed the Hajj. For those not on Hajj, fasting that day is a recommended act.

clues: It is a direction, not an object.
Every Muslim uses it daily.
It was changed during the Madinan period.
It was previously towards Jerusalem.
It is now towards the Ka'bah in Makkah.
medium.explain: The qiblah is the direction of prayer. It was initially toward Jerusalem and was changed to the Ka'bah in Makkah during the Madinan period, an event referred to in Surah Al-Baqarah.

clues: It is a required charity.
It is tied to a particular time of year.
It is due at the end of Ramadan.
It is given on behalf of each member of a household.
It must be given before the Eid prayer.
medium.explain: Zakat al-Fitr is given at the end of Ramadan on behalf of each person in a household, and must reach those entitled to it before the Eid prayer. It is distinct from zakat on wealth.

clues: It is a voluntary prayer.
It is prayed at night.
It is prayed after sleeping, not before.
The last third of the night is the most virtuous time for it.
It is also called qiyam al-layl.
medium.explain: Tahajjud is the voluntary night prayer offered after waking from sleep, most virtuously in the last third of the night. Tarawih, by contrast, is prayed after Isha in Ramadan.

clues: It is a rite of Hajj and Umrah.
It involves walking back and forth.
It is performed seven times.
It takes place between two small hills.
Those hills are Safa and Marwah.
medium.explain: Sa'i is the walking between Safa and Marwah, seven circuits in all. It recalls Hajar's search for water for her son Isma'il.

clues: It is a state a pilgrim enters.
It is entered at a fixed boundary before Makkah.
Certain ordinarily permitted things become forbidden in it.
Men wear two unstitched white cloths.
It is entered before performing Hajj or Umrah.
medium.explain: Ihram is the consecrated state a pilgrim enters at the designated miqat before Makkah, marked for men by two unstitched white garments. Certain normally lawful acts, such as cutting hair or using perfume, are prohibited while in it.

clues: It is a surah of the Qur'an.
It is quite short — seven ayahs.
It is the first surah in the mushaf.
It is recited in every unit of every prayer.
It is known as the Opening.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Fatihah, the Opening, has seven ayahs and is recited in every rak'ah of every prayer. It is also called Umm al-Kitab, the Mother of the Book.

clues: It is a short surah near the end of the Qur'an.
It has four ayahs.
It is entirely about the nature of Allah.
It is said to equal a third of the Qur'an in reward.
It begins: Say, He is Allah, One.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Ikhlas (112) has four ayahs and declares the absolute oneness of Allah. A well-known hadith describes it as equal to a third of the Qur'an in reward.

clues: It is part of Hajj.
It takes place outside Makkah.
It happens on a single day, 9 Dhul-Hijjah.
Missing it means the Hajj is not valid.
It is the standing on the plain of Arafah.
medium.explain: The standing at Arafah on 9 Dhul-Hijjah is the essential pillar of Hajj. The Prophet ﷺ said that Hajj is Arafah — a pilgrim who misses it has missed the Hajj.

clues: They are a group of early Muslims.
They are referred to as a group in the Qur'an.
They were not from Makkah.
They were from Madinah.
Their name means the helpers.
medium.explain: The Ansar were the Muslims of Madinah who received and supported the Muhajirun, the emigrants from Makkah. Their name means 'the helpers'.

clues: They are a group of early Muslims.
They are named as a group in the Qur'an.
They are defined by an action they took.
That action was leaving their homes for faith.
They emigrated from Makkah to Madinah.
medium.explain: The Muhajirun were those who emigrated from Makkah to Madinah for their faith. They are frequently paired in the Qur'an with the Ansar, who received them.

clues: It is a voluntary prayer.
It is prayed in congregation in many mosques.
It is specific to one month of the year.
It is prayed after the Isha prayer.
It is prayed during the nights of Ramadan.
medium.explain: Tarawih is the voluntary night prayer of Ramadan, offered after Isha, commonly in congregation. Scholars differ on the number of rak'ahs, with eight and twenty both well established.

clues: It was a journey.
It took place in a single night.
It began at the Masjid al-Haram in Makkah.
It ended at the Masjid al-Aqsa.
Surah Al-Isra opens by mentioning it.
medium.explain: The Isra is the night journey from the Masjid al-Haram in Makkah to the Masjid al-Aqsa, referred to at the opening of Surah Al-Isra. The Mi'raj is the ascension that followed it.

clues: It is a mosque.
It is not in the Arabian peninsula.
It was the first direction of prayer for the Muslims.
It is mentioned at the beginning of Surah Al-Isra.
It is in Jerusalem.
medium.explain: Masjid al-Aqsa in Jerusalem was the first qiblah, before the direction of prayer was changed to the Ka'bah. It is named at the opening of Surah Al-Isra as the destination of the night journey.

clues: It is a mosque in Madinah.
It is connected with the Hijrah.
It was built very early in the Madinan period.
It is described as the first mosque built in Islam.
The Prophet ﷺ stopped and built it on arriving before entering the city.
medium.explain: Masjid Quba, on the outskirts of Madinah, is generally described as the first mosque built in Islam, established by the Prophet ﷺ on his arrival during the Hijrah.

clues: It refers to a collection, not a single thing.
The Qur'an mentions it by name.
It is about Allah.
It is traditionally counted as ninety-nine.
They are His most beautiful names.
medium.explain: Al-Asma al-Husna are the beautiful names of Allah, traditionally enumerated as ninety-nine. The Qur'an instructs that Allah be called upon by them.

clues: It is a single verse, not a surah.
It is in Surah Al-Baqarah.
It is verse 255 of that surah.
It is widely memorised and recited for protection.
It is known as the Verse of the Throne.
medium.explain: Ayat al-Kursi is Surah Al-Baqarah, verse 255. It describes the sovereignty and knowledge of Allah, and is widely recited after prayers and before sleep.

clues: It is a Makkan surah.
It has 110 ayahs.
It contains four distinct stories.
One concerns young men who slept in a cave for many years.
Many Muslims recite it on Fridays.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Kahf (18) contains the stories of the people of the cave, the man with two gardens, Musa and al-Khidr, and Dhul-Qarnayn. Reciting it on Friday is a widespread practice.

clues: It is a Makkan surah of thirty ayahs.
It opens juz 29.
Its name refers to dominion or sovereignty.
It is commonly recited before sleeping.
It is described as interceding for the one who recites it.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Mulk (67) has thirty ayahs and opens juz 29. It is widely recited before sleep, on the strength of narrations describing it as a protector for its reciter.

clues: He appears in Surah Al-Kahf.
He is not named outright in the Qur'an itself.
A prophet travelled with him to learn.
That prophet was Musa.
He performed three acts whose reasons were explained only at the end.
medium.explain: The figure travelling with Musa in Surah Al-Kahf is identified as al-Khidr in hadith rather than in the Qur'an, which calls him a servant granted knowledge from Allah. Scholars differ over whether he was a prophet.

clues: He appears in Surah Al-Kahf.
He was a powerful and just traveller-ruler.
He journeyed to the west, then to the east.
He encountered a people who asked him for help.
He built a barrier against Ya'juj and Ma'juj.
medium.explain: Dhul-Qarnayn is described in Surah Al-Kahf as a just ruler who built a barrier against Ya'juj and Ma'juj. His historical identity is debated and the Qur'an does not specify it.

clues: A surah of the Qur'an is named after him.
He is not generally counted among the prophets.
He was granted wisdom by Allah.
The surah records his advice to his son.
He warned his son against shirk above all.
medium.explain: Surah Luqman (31) records the counsel of Luqman the Wise to his son, beginning with a warning against shirk. He is generally regarded as a wise man rather than a prophet.

clues: It is a Makkan surah of 83 ayahs.
It is surah 36 in the mushaf.
It is widely memorised and frequently recited.
It is sometimes called the heart of the Qur'an.
Its name consists of two disconnected letters.
medium.explain: Surah Yasin (36) has 83 ayahs. It opens with the disconnected letters Ya-Sin, and is widely recited. Scholars differ on the authenticity of some narrations about its particular merits.

clues: They occur at the start of certain surahs.
There are twenty-nine surahs that begin with them.
They are recited letter by letter, not as words.
Alif-Lam-Mim is the best known example.
Their meaning is known to Allah alone, according to most scholars.
medium.explain: Al-Huruf al-Muqatta'at, the disconnected letters, open twenty-nine surahs. Most scholars hold their meaning to be known to Allah alone, though various interpretations have been offered.

clues: It is a term from the rules of zakat.
It is a quantity, not an action.
Below it, no zakat is due.
It is traditionally measured against gold or silver.
It is the minimum threshold of wealth.
medium.explain: The nisab is the minimum amount of wealth a person must hold before zakat becomes due, traditionally measured against set weights of gold or silver. The hawl is the lunar year that must pass over it.

clues: They are a group of leaders.
They led after the Prophet ﷺ.
There were four of them, by the usual count.
Their period lasted about thirty years.
Their name means the rightly-guided.
medium.explain: The Rashidun, the rightly-guided caliphs, are Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman and Ali, whose combined rule spanned roughly 11 to 40 AH.

clues: It is a Madinan surah.
It is the longest surah in the Qur'an.
It has 286 ayahs.
It contains the longest verse in the Qur'an.
It contains Ayat al-Kursi.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Baqarah (2) is the longest surah at 286 ayahs. It contains Ayat al-Kursi (2:255) and the Qur'an's longest verse, the verse of debt (2:282).

clues: It is a category of narration.
It is transmitted through the Prophet ﷺ.
Its meaning is attributed to Allah.
Its wording is the Prophet's own.
It is nonetheless not part of the Qur'an.
medium.explain: A hadith qudsi conveys meaning attributed to Allah in the Prophet's own wording. It is distinct from the Qur'an, which is revealed in both meaning and exact wording.

clues: It is a technical term in hadith study.
Every narration has one.
It is not the content of the report.
It is examined to judge reliability.
It is the chain of narrators.
medium.explain: The isnad is the chain of narrators through which a hadith is transmitted; the matn is its text. Scholars assess both in grading a narration.

clues: It is a discipline of Islamic scholarship.
It concerns the Qur'an.
It is not about pronunciation.
It draws on language, context and narrations.
It is the explanation of the Qur'an's meaning.
medium.explain: Tafsir is the exegesis of the Qur'an, drawing on language, occasions of revelation, and narrations. Well-known works include those of al-Tabari and Ibn Kathir.

clues: It is a discipline concerning the Qur'an.
It is not about meaning.
It governs how the text is uttered.
It covers elongation, merging and nasalisation.
It is the science of correct recitation.
medium.explain: Tajwid governs the correct pronunciation of the Qur'an — the articulation points of letters and rules such as madd, idgham and ghunnah.

clues: It occurs within the prayer.
It is a supplication, not a movement.
It is most often associated with the Witr prayer.
It is also made at times of calamity.
It is typically made while standing, after rising from ruku.
medium.explain: Qunut is a supplication made while standing in prayer, most commonly in Witr. Schools differ on where and when it is recited.

clues: It is a financial duty in Islamic law.
It is owed to specific people, not the general poor.
It is not an annual calculation.
It concerns those in one's care.
It is the maintenance owed to one's dependants.
medium.explain: Nafaqah is the maintenance a person owes to their dependants — spouse, children and in some cases parents. It is distinct from zakat, which is owed to the eight Qur'anic categories.

clues: It relates to fasting.
It applies to those who cannot fast at all.
It applies, for example, to the chronically ill or the very elderly.
It is not a penalty for deliberate breaking of the fast.
It is feeding a needy person for each missed day.
medium.explain: Fidyah is the compensation of feeding a needy person for each fast a person is permanently unable to keep. Kaffarah is the heavier expiation for deliberately breaking a fast.

clues: It concerns an act of worship not performed on time.
It applies to prayers and to fasts.
It does not involve money.
A traveller or a sick person may need to do it.
It is making up what was missed, later.
medium.explain: Qada is making up a missed obligatory prayer or fast at a later time — for example, fasts missed during Ramadan due to illness or travel.

clues: It belongs to the rules of marriage.
It is given by the husband.
It is given to the wife herself, not her family.
It is her property to keep.
It is a required part of the marriage contract.
medium.explain: The mahr is the dower given by the husband to the wife as her own property. It is a requirement of the marriage contract and belongs to her alone.

clues: It is surah 55.
It falls in juz 27.
It opens with one of the names of Allah.
It enumerates blessings one after another.
A single verse is repeated thirty-one times within it.
medium.explain: Surah Ar-Rahman (55) repeats the refrain 'Then which of the favours of your Lord will you deny?' thirty-one times, between enumerated blessings.

clues: It is a Makkan surah of 96 ayahs.
It is surah 56, falling in juz 27.
Its name refers to an event that must come.
It divides people into three groups.
Those groups are the foremost, the companions of the right, and the companions of the left.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Waqi'ah (56) describes the Inevitable Event and divides humanity into three categories: the foremost, the companions of the right hand, and the companions of the left.

clues: It is the shortest surah in the Qur'an.
It has three ayahs.
It is a Makkan surah.
It was revealed as consolation to the Prophet ﷺ.
Its name refers to abundance granted to him.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Kawthar (108) is the shortest surah at three ayahs. It was revealed as consolation, affirming that it is the Prophet's detractor who is cut off.

clues: It is a form of purification.
It is more complete than the usual ablution.
It is required in specific states.
It involves washing the whole body.
It is recommended before Jumu'ah and the two Eids.
medium.explain: Ghusl is the complete washing of the body, obligatory in certain states and recommended before Jumu'ah, the two Eids and entering ihram.

clues: It is a means of purification.
It is used only in particular circumstances.
It does not involve water at all.
It is permitted when water is unavailable or harmful.
It is performed with clean earth or dust.
medium.explain: Tayammum is dry purification with clean earth, permitted when water is unavailable or its use would cause harm.

clues: It is a Madinan surah of eleven ayahs.
It is surah 62.
It is named after a day.
It commands leaving off trade when the call is made.
It instructs the believers to hasten to the remembrance of Allah.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Jumu'ah (62) commands the believers to leave trade and hasten to the remembrance of Allah when the Friday call to prayer is made.

clues: It is a boundary, not a building.
It concerns pilgrims approaching Makkah.
There are several of them in different directions.
A pilgrim may not pass it in ordinary clothes if intending the rites.
It is where ihram is entered.
medium.explain: The mawaqit are the fixed points around Makkah at which pilgrims coming from different directions must enter the state of ihram.

clues: It is a calendar.
It has twelve months.
Its months are determined by the moon.
Its year is about eleven days shorter than the solar year.
Its count begins from the migration to Madinah.
medium.explain: The Hijri calendar is lunar, with twelve months and a year of about 354 days, counted from the year of the Hijrah in 622 CE.

clues: It was fought between Muslims.
It took place during the first fitnah.
It was in the caliphate of Ali.
It was fought near Basra in 36 AH.
It takes its name from the animal Aisha rode during it.
medium.explain: The Battle of the Camel, 36 AH, was fought near Basra during the first fitnah. It takes its name from the camel on which Aisha was present at the battle.

clues: The term refers to two surahs together.
They are both very short.
They are the final two in the mushaf.
Both begin with the command: Say, I seek refuge.
They are Al-Falaq and An-Nas.
medium.explain: Al-Mu'awwidhatayn, the two surahs of seeking refuge, are Al-Falaq (113) and An-Nas (114), both opening with 'Qul a'udhu'.

clues: It is a rite of Hajj.
It takes place at Mina.
It is performed on the 10th and the days of Tashriq.
It involves small stones.
It is the stoning of the pillars.
medium.explain: Ramy al-Jamarat is the stoning of the three pillars at Mina, performed on the Day of Sacrifice and during the days of Tashriq.

clues: It is a Makkan surah of forty ayahs.
It is surah 78.
It opens the final juz.
Its opening words give that juz its common name.
It begins by asking what they are asking one another about.
medium.explain: Surah An-Naba (78) opens juz 30, which is commonly called Juz Amma after this surah's opening words, 'Amma yatasa'alun'.

clues: It is an alternative name for a surah.
That surah is very short.
It is recited in every unit of prayer.
The name means the Mother of the Book.
The surah is Al-Fatihah.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Fatihah is known by several names, including Umm al-Kitab, the Mother of the Book, and al-Sab' al-Mathani, the seven oft-repeated verses.

clues: It is the gravest matter in Islamic belief.
It concerns the oneness of Allah.
It is the opposite of tawhid.
Luqman warned his son against it above all else.
It is associating partners with Allah.
medium.explain: Shirk is associating partners with Allah, the gravest violation of tawhid. Surah Luqman records his counsel to his son warning against it.

clues: It is a quality of the believer.
The Qur'an states that provisions should be taken, and the best of them is this.
Surah Al-Hujurat says the most honoured are those with most of it.
It is often rendered as God-consciousness.
It is awareness of Allah leading to mindful conduct.
medium.explain: Taqwa is God-consciousness. Surah Al-Hujurat 49:13 states that the most honoured in the sight of Allah is the one with the most taqwa, not the one of highest lineage.

clues: It is a quality of an action, not of a person's knowledge.
It concerns why something is done.
Without it, outward worship is not accepted.
A surah is named with the same word.
It means sincerity, doing an act for Allah alone.
medium.explain: Ikhlas is sincerity of intention — performing an act for Allah alone. The well-known hadith that actions are judged by intentions bears directly on it.

clues: It is a Madinan surah of twenty-nine ayahs.
It is surah 57.
It is named after a material.
It mentions that material being sent down with great strength.
That material is iron.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Hadid (57) is named for iron, which it describes as sent down, containing great strength and benefits for people.

clues: It is a term of disapproval in religious matters.
It concerns worship in particular.
It is contrasted with the established practice.
Scholars discuss its categories in detail.
It refers to newly introduced matters in the religion.
medium.explain: Bid'ah refers to newly introduced practices in religious matters without basis in the sources. Scholars differ considerably over how the term should be applied.

clues: It is one of the six articles of faith.
It is often expressed as a pair of words.
It concerns what Allah has decreed.
It does not remove human responsibility.
It is divine decree and destiny.
medium.explain: Belief in divine decree is the sixth article of faith. Islamic theology holds that it does not negate human responsibility or the reality of choice.

clues: It is a Madinan surah of twenty-two ayahs.
It is surah 58.
Its name refers to a woman.
It was revealed concerning a woman who argued her case.
She brought her complaint about her husband to the Prophet ﷺ.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Mujadilah (58) is named for the woman who disputed her case with the Prophet ﷺ concerning her husband, and whose complaint Allah answered.

clues: It is a quality praised throughout the Qur'an.
It is counselled in Surah Al-Asr.
Prophet Ayyub is its clearest example.
It applies in hardship and in obedience alike.
It is patience and steadfastness.
medium.explain: Sabr is patience and steadfastness — in hardship, in obedience, and in restraint from wrongdoing. Surah Al-Asr names mutual counsel to it as one of four saving qualities.

clues: It was revealed in Madinah.
It begins in juz 6.
It has 120 ayat.
It comes right after Surah An-Nisa in the mushaf.
Its name means “The Table Spread”.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Ma'idah is surah 5 of the mushaf, with 120 ayat, beginning in juz 6. It is a Madani surah.

clues: It was revealed in Makkah.
It begins in juz 7.
It has 165 ayat.
It comes right after Surah Al-Ma'idah in the mushaf.
Its name means “The Cattle”.
medium.explain: Surah Al-An'am is surah 6 of the mushaf, with 165 ayat, beginning in juz 7. It is a Makki surah.

clues: It was revealed in Makkah.
It begins in juz 8.
It has 206 ayat.
It comes right after Surah Al-An'am in the mushaf.
Its name means “The Heights”.
medium.explain: Surah Al-A'raf is surah 7 of the mushaf, with 206 ayat, beginning in juz 8. It is a Makki surah.

clues: It was revealed in Makkah.
It begins in juz 11.
It has 109 ayat.
It comes right after Surah At-Tawbah in the mushaf.
Its name means “Jonah”.
medium.explain: Surah Yunus is surah 10 of the mushaf, with 109 ayat, beginning in juz 11. It is a Makki surah.

clues: It was revealed in Makkah.
It begins in juz 11.
It has 123 ayat.
It comes right after Surah Yunus in the mushaf.
It is named after the prophet sent to the people of 'Ad.
medium.explain: Surah Hud is surah 11 of the mushaf, with 123 ayat, beginning in juz 11. It is a Makki surah.

clues: It was revealed in Makkah.
It begins in juz 13.
It has 52 ayat.
It comes right after Surah Ar-Ra'd in the mushaf.
Its name means “Abraham”.
medium.explain: Surah Ibrahim is surah 14 of the mushaf, with 52 ayat, beginning in juz 13. It is a Makki surah.

clues: It was revealed in Makkah.
It begins in juz 15.
It has 111 ayat.
It comes right after Surah An-Nahl in the mushaf.
Its name means “The Night Journey”.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Isra is surah 17 of the mushaf, with 111 ayat, beginning in juz 15. It is a Makki surah.

clues: It was revealed in Makkah.
It begins in juz 17.
It has 112 ayat.
It comes right after Surah Taha in the mushaf.
Its name means “The Prophets”.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Anbya is surah 21 of the mushaf, with 112 ayat, beginning in juz 17. It is a Makki surah.

clues: It was revealed in Makkah.
It begins in juz 18.
It has 118 ayat.
It comes right after Surah Al-Hajj in the mushaf.
Its name means “The Believers”.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Mu'minun is surah 23 of the mushaf, with 118 ayat, beginning in juz 18. It is a Makki surah.

clues: It was revealed in Madinah.
It begins in juz 18.
It has 64 ayat.
It comes right after Surah Al-Mu'minun in the mushaf.
Its name means “The Light”.
medium.explain: Surah An-Nur is surah 24 of the mushaf, with 64 ayat, beginning in juz 18. It is a Madani surah.

clues: It was revealed in Makkah.
It begins in juz 18.
It has 77 ayat.
It comes right after Surah An-Nur in the mushaf.
Its name means “The Criterion”.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Furqan is surah 25 of the mushaf, with 77 ayat, beginning in juz 18. It is a Makki surah.

clues: It was revealed in Makkah.
It begins in juz 21.

hard.explain: The Year of Sorrow (Am al-Huzn), around 619 CE, is so called because the Prophet ﷺ lost both his wife Khadijah and his uncle Abu Talib within a short period, removing his closest support in Makkah.

clues: It was delivered in the final year of the Prophet's life.
It was given during a pilgrimage.
It was addressed to a very large gathering.
It affirmed the sanctity of life, property and honour.
It stated that no Arab has superiority over a non-Arab except by taqwa.
hard.explain: The Farewell Sermon was delivered during the Farewell Pilgrimage in 10 AH. Among its themes were the sanctity of life and property, the rights of women, the abolition of pre-Islamic blood feuds and usury, and the equality of people regardless of lineage.

clues: It was a pledge of allegiance.
It took place in 6 AH.
It happened outside Makkah, before a treaty was signed.
It was given beneath a tree.
The Qur'an states that Allah was pleased with the believers who gave it.
hard.explain: The Pledge of Ridwan was given beneath a tree at Hudaybiyyah, when a rumour reached the Muslims that Uthman had been killed. Surah Al-Fath refers to Allah being pleased with the believers who pledged under the tree.

clues: It was a formal document.
It dates from very early in the Madinan period.
It was not an agreement with the Quraysh.
It set out relations between the groups living in one city.
It covered the Muhajirun, the Ansar and the Jewish tribes of Madinah.
hard.explain: The Constitution of Madinah was drawn up shortly after the Hijrah, defining the rights and obligations of the Muhajirun, the Ansar and the Jewish tribes as a single community for purposes of defence and mutual obligation.

clues: They were pledges of allegiance.
They took place before the Hijrah.
They were given during the pilgrimage season.
They were given by people from Yathrib, not Makkah.
They prepared the way for the migration to Madinah.
hard.explain: The two Pledges of Aqabah were given by groups from Yathrib during the pilgrimage season in the years before the Hijrah. They established the support base that made the migration to Madinah possible.

clues: It was the first major battle of the Madinan period.
It took place in Ramadan.
The Muslims were heavily outnumbered.
The Qur'an refers to it as the day of distinction, Yawm al-Furqan.
It was fought in 2 AH.
hard.explain: Badr, fought in Ramadan of 2 AH, was the first major engagement between the Muslims of Madinah and the Quraysh. The Qur'an calls it Yawm al-Furqan, the Day of Distinction.

clues: It was fought near a mountain outside Madinah.
It took place the year after a major victory.
A group of archers left their assigned position.
The Prophet ﷺ was wounded during it.
Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib was killed in it.
hard.explain: Uhud, 3 AH, followed Badr. The withdrawal of archers from the hill they had been ordered to hold turned the course of the battle, and Hamza, the Prophet's uncle, was among those killed.

clues: It happened on the same night as another famous event.
It followed the journey to Jerusalem.
It involved rising upward.
The five daily prayers were prescribed during it.
It was the ascension through the heavens.
hard.explain: The Mi'raj is the ascension that followed the Isra on the same night. It is during this that the five daily prayers were prescribed, after an initial command of fifty.

clues: It is a Madinan surah.
It is named for a victory.
It was revealed in connection with a specific episode.
That episode was an agreement many Muslims found disappointing at the time.
It refers to the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah as a manifest victory.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Fath (48) was revealed in connection with the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah, describing it as a manifest victory despite its terms appearing unfavourable to the Muslims at the time.

clues: It is the name of a particular year.
It precedes the Prophet's mission.
It is traditionally placed around the year of his birth.
An army marched on Makkah and failed.
Surah Al-Fil refers to it.
hard.explain: The Year of the Elephant is traditionally placed around the Prophet's birth, about 570 CE. Surah Al-Fil refers to the destruction of the army that advanced on Makkah with an elephant.

clues: It is the name given to a year late in the Prophet's life.
It followed the conquest of Makkah.
It is usually dated to 9 AH.
It is named for groups who travelled to Madinah.
Tribes came from across Arabia to accept Islam.
hard.explain: The Year of Delegations, usually placed at 9 AH, is so called because tribes from across Arabia sent delegations to Madinah to accept Islam following the conquest of Makkah.

clues: It was fought outside the Arabian heartland.
It took place in 8 AH, before the conquest of Makkah.
Three appointed commanders were killed in succession.
Khalid ibn al-Walid took command and withdrew the force.
Zayd ibn Harithah and Ja'far ibn Abi Talib were among those killed.
hard.explain: Mu'tah, 8 AH, was fought near the Byzantine frontier. Zayd ibn Harithah, Ja'far ibn Abi Talib and Abdullah ibn Rawahah were killed in succession, after which Khalid ibn al-Walid took command and extracted the army.

clues: It took place in 9 AH.
It was undertaken in severe heat and hardship.
It was the last major expedition the Prophet ﷺ led in person.
No battle was actually fought.
Three companions who stayed behind were boycotted until their repentance was accepted.
hard.explain: Tabuk, 9 AH, was undertaken in great heat and difficulty and ended without fighting. Surah At-Tawbah addresses those who stayed behind, including the three whose repentance was eventually accepted.

clues: It was fought in 8 AH.
It came very shortly after a major and peaceful success.
The Muslim force was unusually large this time.
Its opening moments went badly despite that advantage.
The Qur'an notes that their numbers pleased them but availed them nothing.
hard.explain: Hunayn followed soon after the conquest of Makkah in 8 AH. Surah At-Tawbah mentions that the Muslims' large numbers pleased them but were of no avail at first, before the situation was retrieved.

clues: It is a Makkan surah.
Its opening verses have a special status.
Those verses were revealed at the cave of Hira.
They were the very first revelation.
They begin with the command: Read.
hard.explain: The first five verses of Surah Al-Alaq (96) were the first revelation, received at the cave of Hira, beginning with the command 'Iqra' — Read.

clues: It is an institution, not an act of worship.
It developed in the early Islamic state.
It dealt with resources rather than law.
It handled revenue and its distribution.
It was the public treasury.
hard.explain: Bayt al-Mal was the public treasury of the early Islamic state, responsible for collecting and distributing public revenues including zakat and other income.

clues: It is a single well-known narration.
It takes the form of questions and answers.
A stranger arrived whom nobody recognised.
He asked about three things in turn.
Those three were Islam, Iman and Ihsan.
hard.explain: In the Hadith of Jibril, narrated from Umar ibn al-Khattab, the angel Jibril came in human form and questioned the Prophet ﷺ about Islam, Iman and Ihsan, and the signs of the Hour. It is recorded in Sahih Muslim and Sahih al-Bukhari.

clues: It is a very short surah, three ayahs.
It is placed near the end of the mushaf.
It is widely held to be among the last revealed.
It speaks of people entering the religion in crowds.
It mentions the help of Allah and the victory having come.
hard.explain: Surah An-Nasr (110) has three ayahs and is widely regarded as among the last surahs revealed. It speaks of the help of Allah and of people entering the religion in multitudes.

clues: It took place in 7 AH.
It followed closely on a treaty.
It concerned a set of fortified settlements north of Madinah.
Ali ibn Abi Talib was given the banner.
The settlements were taken after a siege.
hard.explain: Khaybar, 7 AH, followed the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah. The fortified oasis settlements north of Madinah were taken after a siege, with Ali ibn Abi Talib given the banner.

clues: It was a pledge given before the Hijrah.
It was given by a small group from Yathrib.
It is sometimes called the pledge of the women.
Its terms concerned conduct, not warfare.
Mus'ab ibn Umayr was sent back with them to teach.
hard.explain: The first Pledge of Aqabah committed a small group from Yathrib to belief and to abstaining from specified wrongs, without any undertaking to fight. Mus'ab ibn Umayr returned with them as a teacher.

clues: It is a Madinan surah of 129 ayahs.
It is the ninth surah.
It is the only surah not opened by the Basmalah.
It deals with treaties and with those who stayed behind.
Its themes connect closely with the expedition to Tabuk.
hard.explain: Surah At-Tawbah (9) is the only surah that does not begin with the Basmalah. Much of it addresses the aftermath of Tabuk and the conduct of those who did not join it.

clues: It concerns the written text of the Qur'an.
It took place very shortly after the Prophet's passing.
It was prompted by the deaths of many memorisers in battle.
Umar proposed it and Zayd ibn Thabit carried it out.
It gathered the Qur'an into a single written collection.
hard.explain: After many huffaz were killed at the Battle of Yamamah, Umar urged Abu Bakr to have the Qur'an gathered into one written collection, a task entrusted to Zayd ibn Thabit. Uthman's later work standardised and distributed copies.

clues: It concerns the written text of the Qur'an.
It happened about twenty years after the Prophet's passing.
It was prompted by differences arising in distant regions.
Official copies were produced and sent to the major centres.
Zayd ibn Thabit was again central to the work.
hard.explain: Uthman had standard copies prepared and sent to the main centres of the expanding state, in response to differences in recitation emerging among new Muslims in distant regions.

clues: It was fought after the Prophet's passing.
It took place during the caliphate of Abu Bakr.
It was part of the Ridda campaigns.
Many memorisers of the Qur'an were killed in it.
It prompted the gathering of the Qur'an into one collection.
hard.explain: Yamamah, fought during Abu Bakr's caliphate against the forces of Musaylimah, cost the lives of many huffaz — which directly prompted the written compilation of the Qur'an.

clues: It was fought during the Rashidun period.
It was fought against the Byzantines.
It took place near a river in the Levant.
Khalid ibn al-Walid played a decisive role.
It opened the way to Muslim control of Syria.
hard.explain: Yarmuk, fought around 15 AH against the Byzantines, was decisive in bringing Syria under Muslim control. Khalid ibn al-Walid's command is widely credited for the outcome.

clues: It was fought during Umar's caliphate.
It was fought against the Sasanian empire, not the Byzantines.
It took place in Iraq.
Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas commanded the Muslim force.
It opened the way into Persia.
hard.explain: Qadisiyyah, fought in Iraq under the command of Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas during Umar's caliphate, was decisive against the Sasanian empire.

clues: They were a group in Madinah.

hard.explain: The Ashab al-Suffah were poor companions who lived on a raised, shaded platform at the Prophet's Mosque, devoting themselves to learning. Abu Hurayrah was among them.

clues: The term refers to a group connected to the Prophet ﷺ.

hard.explain: Ahl al-Bayt refers to the household of the Prophet ﷺ, mentioned in Surah Al-Ahzab 33:33. Scholars differ on precisely whom the term encompasses.

clues: It is a Madinan surah of eighteen ayahs.

hard.explain: Surah Al-Hujurat (49) sets out norms of conduct: verifying news, reconciling disputes, avoiding mockery, suspicion and backbiting, and the principle that honour lies in taqwa, not lineage.

clues: It is a field within Qur'anic studies.

It is known in Arabic as asbab al-nuzul.
hard.explain: Asbab al-nuzul records the circumstances in which particular verses were revealed. It assists interpretation, though scholars caution that a verse's ruling is not limited to its occasion.

clues: It was an agreement made in Makkah.

hard.explain: Hilf al-Fudul was a pre-Islamic pact among Makkan clans to support anyone wronged in the city. The Prophet ﷺ participated in his youth and later spoke approvingly of it.

clues: It took place in Makkah before the Hijrah.

hard.explain: The Quraysh imposed a boycott on Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib for roughly three years, its terms written on a document hung in the Ka'bah. The hardship it caused preceded the Year of Sorrow.

clues: It was a journey undertaken from Makkah.

Its purpose was to seek support from another town.
The Prophet ﷺ was rejected and driven out.
He returned saying he complained of his weakness only to Allah.
hard.explain: After the Year of Sorrow, the Prophet ﷺ travelled to Ta'if seeking support and was rejected and pelted. The episode is remembered particularly for his supplication on the return journey.

clues: It is a Madinan surah of twenty-four ayahs.
Its name refers to a gathering or exile.
It praises the Ansar for preferring others over themselves.
It warns against being like those who forgot Allah.
Its final three verses enumerate names of Allah.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Hashr (59) closes with three verses enumerating many of the names and attributes of Allah, and earlier praises the Ansar for preferring others over themselves despite their own need.

clues: It is a concept in Qur'anic and legal study.

Scholars differ considerably over its extent.
It is the abrogation of an earlier ruling by a later one.
hard.explain: Naskh is the abrogation of an earlier ruling by a later revelation. Its existence is broadly accepted, but scholars differ substantially over how many verses it affects.

clues: It is one of the sources of Islamic law.
It ranks after the Qur'an and the Sunnah.
It is not individual reasoning.
It concerns the position of the scholars collectively.
It is consensus.
hard.explain: Ijma is the consensus of qualified scholars, conventionally the third source of law after the Qur'an and Sunnah. Qiyas, analogical reasoning, is usually listed fourth.

clues: It is one of the sources of Islamic law.
It is conventionally listed fourth.
It is used when no direct text addresses a matter.
It extends an existing ruling to a new case.
It works by identifying a shared underlying cause.
hard.explain: Qiyas is analogical reasoning: extending a ruling from a case addressed by the texts to a new case sharing the same effective cause ('illah). The Zahiri school rejected it.

clues: It is a very short Makkan surah.
It has three ayahs.
It opens with an oath.
It states that mankind is in loss, with exceptions.
Al-Shafi'i said that if people reflected on it alone it would suffice them.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Asr (103) has three ayahs: an oath by time, the declaration that mankind is in loss, and the four exceptions — faith, righteous deeds, and mutual counsel to truth and to patience.

clues: It was a period of internal conflict.
It followed the killing of a caliph.
It fell within the caliphate of Ali.
It included the Battle of the Camel.

hard.explain: The first fitnah was the civil conflict following the killing of Uthman, encompassing the Battle of the Camel in 36 AH and Siffin in 37 AH during Ali's caliphate.

clues: They took place immediately after the Prophet's passing.

They concerned tribes withdrawing from the new state.
They included the Battle of Yamamah.
They ended with the peninsula reunified.
hard.explain: The Ridda campaigns under Abu Bakr addressed tribes that withheld allegiance or zakat after the Prophet's passing. The Battle of Yamamah was their costliest engagement.

clues: It is a Madinan surah of seventy-three ayahs.
It is surah 33.
Its name refers to a confederacy.
It relates to the siege of Madinah.
It also contains the verse naming the Prophet ﷺ as the seal of the prophets.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Ahzab (33) is named for the Confederates who besieged Madinah at Khandaq. It contains 33:40, naming the Prophet ﷺ as the Seal of the Prophets.

clues: He was among the earliest Muslims.
He is one of the ten given glad tidings.
He emigrated twice, to Abyssinia and then Madinah.
He was known for great wealth and generosity.
Umar appointed him to the council that chose the next caliph.
hard.explain: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf was among the earliest Muslims and the ten promised Paradise, known for his wealth and generosity, and a member of the shura Umar appointed to select his successor.

clues: It was a council convened to make a decision.

Its outcome was the caliphate of Uthman.
hard.explain: Umar appointed a council of six senior companions to choose his successor from among themselves. Their deliberation resulted in the selection of Uthman.

clues: It was a gathering in Madinah.

Abu Bakr, Umar and Abu Ubaydah arrived during it.

hard.explain: The gathering at the Saqifah of Banu Sa'idah immediately after the Prophet's passing concluded with the pledge of allegiance to Abu Bakr as the first caliph.

clues: It is a Madinan surah of seventy-five ayahs.
It is surah 8.
Its name refers to the spoils of war.
It was revealed largely in connection with one battle.
That battle is Badr.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Anfal (8) relates largely to the Battle of Badr and its aftermath, including the distribution of spoils. It is followed by At-Tawbah, the only surah without the Basmalah.

clues: It is a traditional grouping of surahs.

hard.explain: Al-Mufassal is the final section of the mushaf, comprising the shorter surahs. Scholars differ on its starting point, commonly given as Surah Qaf or Al-Hujurat.

clues: It is a traditional grouping of surahs.

hard.explain: Al-Sab' al-Tiwal are the seven long surahs beginning at Al-Baqarah. The seventh is counted either as Al-Anfal with At-Tawbah together, or as Yunus.

clues: He was an uncle of the Prophet ﷺ.

hard.explain: Abu Talib raised and protected the Prophet ﷺ through the difficult Makkan years. His death, alongside Khadijah's, gave the Year of Sorrow its name.

clues: He was a leading figure of the Quraysh.

hard.explain: Surah Al-Mumtahanah (60) addresses loyalty and relations with those outside the community, and the examination of women who emigrated to Madinah.

hard.explain: Ibn Khaldun (d. 1406) is best known for the Muqaddimah, the introduction to his universal history, widely regarded as a foundational work in historiography and social thought.
