It begins in juz 24.
It has 54 ayat.
It comes right after Surah Ghafir in the mushaf.
Its name means “Explained in Detail”.
hard.explain: Surah Fussilat is surah 41 of the mushaf, with 54 ayat, beginning in juz 24. It is a Makki surah.

clues: It was revealed in Makkah.
It begins in juz 25.
It has 53 ayat.
It comes right after Surah Fussilat in the mushaf.
Its name means “The Consultation”.
hard.explain: Surah Ash-Shuraa is surah 42 of the mushaf, with 53 ayat, beginning in juz 25. It is a Makki surah.

clues: It was revealed in Makkah.
It begins in juz 25.
It has 89 ayat.
It comes right after Surah Ash-Shuraa in the mushaf.
Its name means “The Ornaments of Gold”.
hard.explain: Surah Az-Zukhruf is surah 43 of the mushaf, with 89 ayat, beginning in juz 25. It is a Makki surah.

clues: It was revealed in Makkah.
It begins in juz 25.
It has 59 ayat.
It comes right after Surah Az-Zukhruf in the mushaf.
Its name means “The Smoke”.
hard.explain: Surah Ad-Dukhan is surah 44 of the mushaf, with 59 ayat, beginning in juz 25. It is a Makki surah.

clues: It was revealed in Makkah.
It begins in juz 25.
It has 37 ayat.
It comes right after Surah Ad-Dukhan in the mushaf.
Its name means “The Crouching”.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Jathiyah is surah 45 of the mushaf, with 37 ayat, beginning in juz 25. It is a Makki surah.

clues: It was revealed in Makkah.
It begins in juz 26.
It has 35 ayat.
It comes right after Surah Al-Jathiyah in the mushaf.
Its name means “The Wind-Curved Sandhills”.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Ahqaf is surah 46 of the mushaf, with 35 ayat, beginning in juz 26. It is a Makki surah.

statements: The Qur'an has 114 surahs.
Surah Al-Fatihah has seven ayahs.
The Qur'an was revealed to Prophet Musa.
easy.explain: The Qur'an was revealed to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ. Musa received the Tawrat. The other two statements are correct.

statements: There are five obligatory prayers each day.
Ramadan is the ninth month of the Islamic calendar.
Hajj is performed in the month of Rajab.
easy.explain: Hajj is performed in Dhul-Hijjah, the twelfth month. Umrah may be performed at any time of year, which is sometimes the source of the confusion.

statements: The Ka'bah is in Makkah.
Muslims face the Ka'bah during prayer.
The Ka'bah was built by Prophet Musa.
easy.explain: The Qur'an describes Ibrahim and his son Isma'il raising the foundations of the Ka'bah. Musa is not connected with its construction.

statements: Zakat is one of the five pillars of Islam.
Fasting the month of Ramadan is obligatory.
There are seven pillars of Islam.
easy.explain: There are five pillars: the shahada, salah, zakat, fasting Ramadan, and Hajj for those able.

statements: The first revelation came while the Prophet ﷺ was at the cave of Hira.
The Prophet ﷺ migrated from Makkah to Madinah.
The Prophet ﷺ passed away in Makkah.
easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ passed away in Madinah, in 11 AH, and is buried there.

statements: Surah Al-Fatihah is recited in every unit of prayer.
The Qur'an was revealed in Arabic.
The Qur'an was revealed all at once in a single night.
easy.explain: The Qur'an was revealed in stages over approximately 23 years. What is described as happening in a single blessed night is the beginning of its revelation.

statements: Muslims fast during the month of Ramadan.
The fast begins at dawn and ends at sunset.
The fast begins at sunset and ends at dawn.
easy.explain: The fast runs from the break of dawn until sunset. Eating is permitted during the night.

statements: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ was born in Makkah.
The Qur'an was revealed in Arabic.
The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ could not be described as a messenger.
easy.explain: The Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is a messenger of Allah; affirming this is part of the shahada itself.

statements: There are 114 surahs in the Qur'an.
Surah Al-Baqarah is the longest surah.
Surah Al-Baqarah is the first surah in the mushaf.
easy.explain: Al-Fatihah is the first surah. Al-Baqarah is the second, and the longest at 286 ayahs.

statements: Eid al-Fitr comes at the end of Ramadan.
Eid al-Adha comes during the month of Hajj.
Eid al-Adha comes at the end of Ramadan.
easy.explain: Eid al-Fitr ends Ramadan, on 1 Shawwal. Eid al-Adha falls on 10 Dhul-Hijjah, during the days of Hajj.

statements: Muslims pray facing the Ka'bah.
The Ka'bah is in Makkah.
Muslims pray facing Madinah.
easy.explain: The qiblah is the Ka'bah in Makkah, not Madinah. Madinah holds the Prophet's mosque but is not the direction of prayer.

statements: Zakat is given to those in need.
Zakat is one of the five pillars.
Zakat is a voluntary charity with no fixed rules.
easy.explain: Zakat is obligatory, with a defined threshold (nisab), rate and set of eligible recipients. The voluntary charity is sadaqah.

statements: Jumu'ah prayer is held on Friday.
Jumu'ah is preceded by a sermon.
Jumu'ah prayer is held on Saturday.
easy.explain: Jumu'ah is the Friday congregational prayer, and it is preceded by the khutbah.

statements: Wudu is performed before prayer.
Wudu involves washing the face, arms and feet.
Wudu is performed only once a year.
easy.explain: Wudu is performed whenever it has been invalidated and prayer is to be offered — potentially several times a day.

statements: The Qur'an was revealed to Prophet Muhammad ﷺ.
The Tawrat was given to Prophet Musa.
The Zabur was given to Prophet Isa.
easy.explain: The Zabur was given to Prophet Dawud. Prophet Isa was given the Injil.

statements: Hajj is performed in Dhul-Hijjah.
Umrah can be performed at any time of year.
Hajj can be performed at any time of year.
easy.explain: Hajj has a fixed season in Dhul-Hijjah. It is Umrah that may be performed at any time.

statements: Fajr is prayed before sunrise.
Maghrib is prayed after sunset.
Isha is prayed before Maghrib.
easy.explain: Isha comes after Maghrib. The order through the day is Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha.

statements: The Ka'bah is a cube-shaped structure.
Pilgrims walk around the Ka'bah seven times.
Pilgrims walk around the Ka'bah three times.
easy.explain: Tawaf consists of seven circuits around the Ka'bah.

statements: Angels are created beings.
Jibril brought revelation to the prophets.
Jibril was a prophet sent to his own people.
easy.explain: Jibril is an angel, not a prophet. Prophets are human beings chosen from among their own people.

statements: Surah Al-Fatihah is recited in every rak'ah.
Surah Al-Fatihah has seven ayahs.
Surah Al-Fatihah is the last surah in the Qur'an.
easy.explain: Al-Fatihah is the first surah. The last is An-Nas, surah 114.

statements: The shahada has two parts.
Saying the shahada sincerely is how one enters Islam.
The shahada is one of the pillars of iman.
easy.explain: The shahada is the first of the five pillars of Islam. The articles of iman are a separate list of six beliefs.

statements: Prophet Nuh built an ark.
Prophet Musa was given the Tawrat.
Prophet Nuh was given the Tawrat.
easy.explain: The Tawrat was given to Musa. No scripture is named in the Qur'an as having been given to Nuh.

statements: Maryam is the mother of Prophet Isa.
Maryam is named in the Qur'an.
Maryam was a prophet.
easy.explain: Maryam is honoured as chosen above the women of the worlds, and a surah bears her name, but she is not counted among the prophets.

statements: Muslims greet one another with as-salamu alaykum.
The greeting means peace be upon you.
The greeting is only used once a year.
easy.explain: The greeting of peace is used in everyday life, whenever Muslims meet.

statements: Fasting is obligatory during Ramadan.
Children before puberty are not obliged to fast.
Everyone without exception must fast, including the seriously ill.
easy.explain: The Qur'an exempts the sick and the traveller, who make up the days later; those permanently unable to fast give fidyah instead.

statements: The Qur'an has 114 surahs.
Surah An-Nas is the last surah.
Surah An-Nas is the first surah.
easy.explain: An-Nas is surah 114, the last. Al-Fatihah is the first.

statements: Hajj takes place in Makkah.
Tawaf is performed around the Ka'bah.
Tawaf is performed around Mount Arafah.
easy.explain: Tawaf is the circling of the Ka'bah. Arafah is a plain where pilgrims stand on the 9th of Dhul-Hijjah; there is no circling there.

statements: Angels are created from light, according to hadith.
Angels do not disobey Allah.
Angels are a kind of prophet.
easy.explain: Angels and prophets are entirely distinct. Prophets are human beings chosen from among people.

statements: Muslims believe in all the prophets.
Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is the final prophet.
Prophet Muhammad ﷺ is the first prophet.
easy.explain: Adam, ʿalayhi al-salām, is the first. Muhammad ﷺ is the final prophet, the seal of the prophets.

statements: Salah is performed five times a day.
Each salah has a set number of rak'ahs.
Each of the five prayers has the same number of rak'ahs.
easy.explain: Fajr has two rak'ahs, Maghrib three, and Dhuhr, Asr and Isha four each.

statements: The Qur'an is the word of Allah.
It was revealed through the angel Jibril.
It was written by the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ himself.
easy.explain: The Qur'an is revelation, not authorship. It was conveyed through Jibril, memorised and recorded by scribes among the companions.

statements: A mosque is a place of worship.
The imam leads the congregational prayer.
The imam must be an angel.
easy.explain: The imam is a person who leads the prayer; any qualified Muslim man may do so.

statements: Zakat helps those in need.
Sadaqah is voluntary.
Sadaqah is obligatory and zakat is voluntary.
easy.explain: It is the other way round: zakat is obligatory with fixed rules, while sadaqah is voluntary.

statements: Laylat al-Qadr falls in Ramadan.
Eid al-Fitr falls in Shawwal.
Laylat al-Qadr falls in Shawwal.
easy.explain: Laylat al-Qadr is sought in the last ten nights of Ramadan. Shawwal is the month that follows, beginning with Eid al-Fitr.

statements: Prophet Ibrahim is associated with the Ka'bah.
Prophet Isma'il was his son.
Prophet Musa was his son.
easy.explain: Isma'il and Ishaq were sons of Ibrahim. Musa came many generations later.

statements: The adhan is the call to prayer.
It is called before each obligatory prayer.
It is called only on Fridays.
easy.explain: The adhan precedes each of the five daily prayers, every day.

statements: Muslims fast from food and drink while fasting.
The fast is broken at sunset.
The fast is broken at midnight.
easy.explain: The fast ends at sunset with iftar, at the time of the Maghrib prayer.

statements: Surah Al-Fatihah opens the Qur'an.
It is recited in every rak'ah.
It has seventy ayahs.
easy.explain: Surah Al-Fatihah has seven ayahs, not seventy.

statements: Jibril brought the first revelation.
The first revelation came at the cave of Hira.
The first revelation came in Madinah.
easy.explain: The first revelation came at the cave of Hira, near Makkah, years before the migration to Madinah.

statements: Wudu can be invalidated and then repeated.
Ghusl is a full bath required in certain states.
Ghusl and wudu are exactly the same thing.
easy.explain: Wudu is the partial ablution before prayer; ghusl is the complete washing of the body required in specific states of impurity.

statements: Believing in the angels is an article of faith.
Believing in the Last Day is an article of faith.
Believing in the five pillars is one of the six articles of faith.
easy.explain: The five pillars are acts of Islam, not items in the list of six beliefs. The six articles are Allah, angels, books, messengers, the Last Day, and divine decree.

statements: Prophet Sulayman was a king as well as a prophet.
Prophet Dawud was given the Zabur.
Prophet Sulayman was given the Zabur.
easy.explain: The Zabur was given to Dawud, the father of Sulayman.

statements: Prophet Yunus was swallowed by a great fish.
Prophet Ayyub is known for his patience.
Prophet Ayyub was swallowed by a great fish.
easy.explain: That was Yunus. Ayyub is remembered for patience through severe illness and loss.

statements: Adam was the first human being.
Muhammad ﷺ is the final prophet.
Adam was the final prophet.
easy.explain: Adam, ʿalayhi al-salām, was the first. Muhammad ﷺ is the seal of the prophets.

statements: The Qur'an is divided into 30 ajza.
Many people read one juz a night in Ramadan.
The Qur'an is divided into 30 surahs.
easy.explain: The Qur'an has 114 surahs. It is the juz divisions that number thirty.

statements: Jannah is the reward of the believers.
Jahannam is a place of punishment.
Jannah is a place of punishment.
easy.explain: Jannah is paradise; Jahannam is the Fire.

statements: Iblis refused to prostrate to Adam.
Iblis was of the jinn.
Iblis was one of the angels.
easy.explain: The Qur'an states explicitly that Iblis was of the jinn. Angels do not disobey what they are commanded.

statements: SubhanAllah is a phrase of remembrance.
Alhamdulillah means all praise is for Allah.
Alhamdulillah means Allah is the Greatest.
easy.explain: Allahu akbar means Allah is the Greatest. Alhamdulillah is praise.

statements: A hafiz has memorised the whole Qur'an.
The imam leads the prayer.
A hafiz is someone who leads the prayer.
easy.explain: A hafiz is a memoriser of the Qur'an. Leading the prayer is the role of the imam, though a hafiz often does so.

statements: Halal means permitted.
Haram means forbidden.
Halal means forbidden.
easy.explain: Halal is the permitted and haram the forbidden — the two are opposites.

statements: Prophet Harun was the brother of Musa.
Prophet Isma'il was a son of Ibrahim.
Prophet Harun was a son of Ibrahim.
easy.explain: Harun was the brother of Musa, many generations after Ibrahim.

statements: The mihrab shows the direction of prayer.
The minbar is used for the sermon.
The minbar shows the direction of prayer.
easy.explain: The mihrab is the niche marking the qiblah; the minbar is the pulpit.

statements: Zakat al-Fitr is given before the Eid prayer.
Zakat al-Mal is calculated on wealth.
Zakat al-Fitr is calculated on wealth.
easy.explain: Zakat al-Fitr is a fixed amount per person. Zakat al-Mal is the one calculated against wealth and the nisab.

statements: Tayammum uses clean earth.
Tayammum is used when water is unavailable.
Tayammum is performed with water.
easy.explain: Tayammum is specifically the dry alternative to wudu, used when water is unavailable or harmful.

statements: Prophet Isa was given the Injil.
Prophet Musa was given the Tawrat.
Prophet Isa was given the Tawrat.
easy.explain: The Tawrat was given to Musa and the Injil to Isa, ʿalayhim al-salām.

statements: Qiyam is the standing position in prayer.
Sujud is prostration.
Qiyam is prostration.
easy.explain: Qiyam is standing; sujud is prostration.

statements: Prophet Nuh's people were destroyed by a flood.
Prophet Nuh built an ark.
Prophet Nuh's people were destroyed by an earthquake.
easy.explain: The punishment of Nuh's people was the flood, from which those with him in the ark were saved.

statements: Istighfar is seeking forgiveness.
Takbir is saying Allahu akbar.
Istighfar is saying Allahu akbar.
easy.explain: Istighfar is seeking forgiveness, commonly Astaghfirullah. Takbir is Allahu akbar.

statements: Surah Al-Kawthar is the shortest surah.
Surah Al-Baqarah is the longest.
Surah Al-Kawthar is the longest surah.
easy.explain: Al-Kawthar has three ayahs; Al-Baqarah has 286.

statements: Prophet Yusuf was thrown into a well by his brothers.
A surah is named after Yusuf.
Prophet Yusuf was thrown into a well by his father.
easy.explain: It was his brothers. His father Ya'qub grieved his loss for many years.

statements: Maryam is the mother of Isa.
Surah Maryam is named after her.
Maryam is the mother of Musa.
easy.explain: Maryam is the mother of Isa, ʿalayhi al-salām.

statements: Surah Al-Baqarah has 286 ayahs.
Surah Al-Kawthar has three ayahs.
Surah An-Nas has seven ayahs.
medium.explain: Surah An-Nas has six ayahs. Al-Baqarah is the longest surah at 286, and Al-Kawthar the shortest at three.

statements: The Hijrah took place in 622 CE.
The Islamic calendar counts its years from the Hijrah.
The Hijrah was a migration from Madinah to Makkah.
medium.explain: The direction was the other way: from Makkah to Madinah. Makkah was conquered later, in 8 AH.

statements: The Battle of Badr took place in 2 AH.
The Battle of Uhud took place in 3 AH.
The Battle of Khandaq took place in 2 AH.
medium.explain: Khandaq (the Trench) took place in 5 AH, roughly three years after Badr.

statements: Zakat is commonly 2.5% on qualifying savings held for a lunar year.
Zakat al-Fitr is given before the Eid prayer.
Zakat on savings is due every month.
medium.explain: Zakat on wealth is an annual obligation, due once a lunar year has passed on wealth above the nisab — not monthly.

statements: Surah Al-Ikhlas has four ayahs.
Surah Al-Fatihah is sometimes called Umm al-Kitab.
Surah Yasin is part of juz 30.
medium.explain: Surah Yasin is surah 36 and falls in juz 22–23. Juz 30 begins at Surah An-Naba, surah 78.

statements: Abu Bakr was the first of the Rashidun caliphs.
Umar ibn al-Khattab succeeded Abu Bakr.
Ali ibn Abi Talib was the second caliph.
medium.explain: Ali was the fourth Rashidun caliph. The order was Abu Bakr, Umar, Uthman, then Ali.

statements: Surah Al-Kahf is often recited on Fridays.
Surah Al-Kahf has 110 ayahs.
Surah Al-Kahf is a Madinan surah.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Kahf is Makkan. It has 110 ayahs and is commonly recited on Fridays.

statements: Juz 30 begins with Surah An-Naba.
The Qur'an is divided into 30 ajza.
The Qur'an is divided into 40 ajza.
medium.explain: The Qur'an is conventionally divided into 30 ajza, the thirtieth beginning at Surah An-Naba.

statements: Al-Fatihah has seven ayahs.
Al-Kawthar has three ayahs.
Al-Ikhlas has six ayahs.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Ikhlas has four ayahs. Al-Kawthar, with three, is the shortest surah.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ was about forty at the first revelation.
Revelation continued for about twenty-three years.
Revelation continued for about ten years.
medium.explain: Revelation continued for approximately twenty-three years: roughly thirteen in Makkah and ten in Madinah.

statements: The Makkan period lasted about thirteen years.
The Madinan period lasted about ten years.
The Madinan period lasted about twenty years.
medium.explain: The Madinan period ran from the Hijrah in 622 CE to the Prophet's passing in 632 CE — about ten years.

statements: Eid al-Adha falls on 10 Dhul-Hijjah.
The Day of Arafah falls on 9 Dhul-Hijjah.
The Day of Arafah falls on 10 Dhul-Hijjah.
medium.explain: Arafah is 9 Dhul-Hijjah; Eid al-Adha is the following day, the 10th.

statements: Surah Yasin is surah 36.
Surah Ar-Rahman is surah 55.
Surah Al-Mulk is surah 77.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Mulk is surah 67. Surah 77 is Al-Mursalat.

statements: Sa'i is performed between Safa and Marwah.
Sa'i consists of seven circuits.
Sa'i is performed around the Ka'bah.
medium.explain: Walking around the Ka'bah is Tawaf. Sa'i is the seven circuits between the hills of Safa and Marwah.

statements: Masjid al-Aqsa was the first qiblah.
The qiblah was changed to the Ka'bah in the Madinan period.
The qiblah was changed to the Ka'bah before the Hijrah.
medium.explain: The change of qiblah took place after the Hijrah, during the Madinan period, and is referred to in Surah Al-Baqarah.

statements: Abu Bakr was given the title as-Siddiq.
Umar ibn al-Khattab was given the title al-Faruq.
Uthman ibn Affan was given the title al-Faruq.
medium.explain: Al-Faruq was the title of Umar. Uthman is known as Dhun-Nurayn, the possessor of two lights.

statements: Surah At-Tawbah does not open with the Basmalah.
Surah At-Tawbah is a Madinan surah.
Surah At-Tawbah is the shortest surah in the Qur'an.
medium.explain: At-Tawbah has 129 ayahs and is one of the longer surahs. The shortest is Al-Kawthar.

statements: There are six articles of faith.
There are five pillars of Islam.
There are six pillars of Islam.
medium.explain: There are five pillars of Islam and six articles of iman. The six is the articles of faith, not the pillars.

statements: Laylat al-Qadr is sought in the last ten nights of Ramadan.
Surah Al-Qadr describes it as better than a thousand months.
Laylat al-Qadr falls on a fixed, known date every year.
medium.explain: Its exact night is not fixed in the sources. It is sought across the last ten nights, most commonly on the odd-numbered ones.

statements: Zakat is commonly 2.5% on qualifying savings.
Zakat becomes due after a lunar year has passed.
Zakat is due on all wealth, with no minimum threshold.
medium.explain: Zakat is due only on wealth above the nisab threshold. Below it, no zakat is owed.

statements: The Hijri calendar is lunar.
The Hijri year is shorter than the Gregorian year.
The Hijri year is longer than the Gregorian year.
medium.explain: A lunar year is roughly 354 days, about eleven days shorter than the Gregorian year — which is why Ramadan moves earlier each year.

statements: Surah Al-Kahf contains the story of the people of the cave.
Surah Al-Kahf contains the story of Dhul-Qarnayn.
Surah Al-Kahf contains the story of Yusuf.
medium.explain: The story of Yusuf is told in Surah Yusuf (12). Al-Kahf contains the cave sleepers, the two gardens, Musa and al-Khidr, and Dhul-Qarnayn.

statements: Surah Maryam is surah 19.
Surah Luqman is surah 31.
Surah Yusuf is surah 10.
medium.explain: Surah Yusuf is surah 12. Surah 10 is Yunus.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ was about forty when revelation began.
He lived about twenty-three years after that.
He lived about forty years after that.
medium.explain: Revelation lasted about twenty-three years, and the Prophet ﷺ was around sixty-three at his passing.

statements: Khadijah was the first to believe in the Prophet's message.
Khadijah died before the Hijrah.
Khadijah died after the conquest of Makkah.
medium.explain: Khadijah died around 619 CE in the Year of Sorrow, some three years before the Hijrah and eleven before the conquest of Makkah.

statements: Zakat is due once a lunar year has passed on qualifying wealth.
The nisab is the minimum threshold for zakat.
The nisab is the rate at which zakat is paid.
medium.explain: The nisab is the threshold of wealth; the rate on most savings is 2.5%.

statements: Surah Al-Ikhlas is about the oneness of Allah.
Surah Al-Kafirun addresses the disbelievers of Makkah.
Surah Al-Ikhlas is the longest surah in juz 30.
medium.explain: Al-Ikhlas has four ayahs and is among the shortest. The longest surah in juz 30 is An-Naba, with forty.

statements: The Ansar were from Madinah.
The Muhajirun emigrated from Makkah.
The Ansar emigrated from Makkah.
medium.explain: The Ansar were the helpers of Madinah who received the Muhajirun, the emigrants from Makkah.

statements: Tarawih is prayed in Ramadan.
Tahajjud is prayed after sleeping.
Tarawih is prayed before the Isha prayer.
medium.explain: Tarawih follows Isha. It is not prayed before it.

statements: The Qur'an has 30 ajza.
Juz 30 is called Juz Amma.
Juz 1 is called Juz Amma.
medium.explain: Juz Amma is the thirtieth, named after the opening words of Surah An-Naba, 'Amma yatasa'alun'.

statements: Sa'i is performed seven times between Safa and Marwah.
Tawaf is seven circuits of the Ka'bah.
Sa'i is performed three times.
medium.explain: Both Tawaf and Sa'i consist of seven, not three.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ had a daughter named Fatimah.
Fatimah married Ali ibn Abi Talib.
Fatimah married Uthman ibn Affan.
medium.explain: Fatimah married Ali ibn Abi Talib. Uthman married two of the Prophet's other daughters in succession, which is why he is called Dhun-Nurayn.

statements: Surah Al-Baqarah contains Ayat al-Kursi.
Ayat al-Kursi is verse 255.
Ayat al-Kursi is a complete surah.
medium.explain: Ayat al-Kursi is a single verse within Surah Al-Baqarah, not a surah in its own right.

statements: The Hijri year has twelve months.
The Hijri calendar follows the moon.
The Hijri calendar follows the sun.
medium.explain: The Hijri calendar is lunar, which is why its months shift relative to the solar seasons.

statements: Umar ibn al-Khattab was the second caliph.
Umar accepted Islam in Makkah before the Hijrah.
Umar was the first caliph.
medium.explain: Abu Bakr was the first caliph; Umar succeeded him in 13 AH.

statements: Isa is called al-Masih in the Qur'an.
The Qur'an says Isa was raised up rather than killed.
The Qur'an says Isa was the son of Allah.
medium.explain: The Qur'an explicitly rejects this, affirming that Isa is a servant and messenger of Allah.

statements: The first qiblah was Jerusalem.
The qiblah changed to the Ka'bah.
The qiblah changed from the Ka'bah to Jerusalem.
medium.explain: The change ran the other way: from Jerusalem to the Ka'bah, during the Madinan period.

statements: Hajj has a fixed season.
Ihram is entered at a boundary called the miqat.
Ihram may be entered at any point, including inside Makkah, for Hajj from outside.
medium.explain: Those coming from outside enter ihram at the designated miqat before crossing into the sacred precinct.

statements: Abu Bakr accompanied the Prophet ﷺ on the Hijrah.
They sheltered in the cave of Thawr.
They sheltered in the cave of Hira.
medium.explain: Hira is where the first revelation came, before the Hijrah. The cave on the migration journey was Thawr.

statements: A hadith has a chain of narrators and a text.
The chain is called the isnad.
The chain is called the matn.
medium.explain: The isnad is the chain of narrators; the matn is the text of the report.

statements: Surah Al-Fatihah is called Umm al-Kitab.
Surah Al-Baqarah is the longest surah.
Surah Al-Fatihah is the longest surah.
medium.explain: Al-Fatihah has seven ayahs. Al-Baqarah, with 286, is the longest.

statements: Surah Al-Waqi'ah is surah 56.
Surah Al-Hadid is surah 57.
Surah Al-Mujadilah is surah 59.
medium.explain: Al-Mujadilah is surah 58. Surah 59 is Al-Hashr.

statements: Ghusl is the full washing of the body.
Wudu is the partial ablution.
Ghusl is required before every prayer.
medium.explain: Wudu is required before prayer. Ghusl is obligatory only in specific states.

statements: The Battle of the Camel was fought in Ali's caliphate.
Siffin was fought in Ali's caliphate.
The Battle of the Camel was fought in the Prophet's lifetime.
medium.explain: Both battles belong to the first fitnah, after the Prophet's passing, during Ali's caliphate.

statements: Al-Mu'awwidhatayn are Al-Falaq and An-Nas.
Both begin with 'Qul a'udhu'.
Al-Mu'awwidhatayn are Al-Ikhlas and Al-Falaq.
medium.explain: The two surahs of seeking refuge are Al-Falaq (113) and An-Nas (114). Al-Ikhlas precedes them.

statements: Juz 29 begins with Surah Al-Mulk.
Juz 30 begins with Surah An-Naba.
Juz 29 begins with Surah An-Naba.
medium.explain: An-Naba opens juz 30. Juz 29 begins with Al-Mulk.

statements: The miqat is where pilgrims enter ihram.
There are several mawaqit in different directions.
The miqat is the plain where pilgrims stand on the 9th.
medium.explain: That plain is Arafah. The mawaqit are boundary points where ihram is entered.

statements: Ramy al-Jamarat takes place at Mina.
Tawaf takes place at the Masjid al-Haram.
Ramy al-Jamarat takes place at Arafah.
medium.explain: The stoning of the pillars takes place at Mina, not Arafah.

statements: Surah Al-Jumu'ah is surah 62.
It commands leaving trade when the call is made.
It is a Makkan surah.
medium.explain: Surah Al-Jumu'ah is Madinan, as the Friday congregational prayer was established in Madinah.

statements: Taqwa is often rendered as God-consciousness.
Surah Al-Hujurat says the most honoured have the most taqwa.
Surah Al-Hujurat says the most honoured have the noblest lineage.
medium.explain: Al-Hujurat 49:13 states the opposite: honour lies in taqwa, not lineage.

statements: Shirk is associating partners with Allah.
Tawhid is the oneness of Allah.
Shirk and tawhid mean the same thing.
medium.explain: They are direct opposites: tawhid affirms oneness, shirk violates it.

statements: Surah An-Naba has 40 ayahs.
Surah An-Naba opens juz 30.
Surah An-Naba is a Madinan surah.
medium.explain: Surah An-Naba is Makkan, like most of juz 30.

statements: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf was among the ten promised Paradise.
Umar appointed a council of six to choose his successor.
Umar appointed a council of ten to choose his successor.
medium.explain: The shura Umar appointed consisted of six senior companions.

statements: Sabr means patience.
Shukr means gratitude.
Sabr means gratitude.
medium.explain: Sabr is patience and steadfastness; shukr is gratitude.

statements: Surah Al-Hadid is named after iron.
It is surah 57.
It is named after a prophet.
medium.explain: Al-Hadid means 'the iron'. It is not named after a person.

statements: The Hijri calendar has twelve months.
Its first month is Muharram.
Its first month is Ramadan.
medium.explain: The year begins with Muharram. Ramadan is the ninth month.

statements: Umm Salamah had migrated to Abyssinia.
She gave decisive counsel at Hudaybiyyah.
She was the first wife of the Prophet ﷺ.
medium.explain: Khadijah was the Prophet's first wife. Umm Salamah married him in Madinah after the death of her husband Abu Salamah.

statements: Ikhlas means sincerity of intention.
Actions are judged by intentions, per a well-known hadith.
Ikhlas means patience in hardship.
medium.explain: Patience is sabr. Ikhlas is doing an act purely for Allah.

statements: Surah Al-Mujadilah concerns a woman who argued her case.
It is surah 58.
It concerns a woman who led an army.
medium.explain: The surah is named for the woman who disputed with the Prophet ﷺ concerning her husband.

statements: Zakat is due after a lunar year on qualifying wealth.
The nisab is the minimum threshold.
Zakat is due immediately on receiving any income.
medium.explain: Zakat on wealth requires a lunar year to pass over holdings above the nisab.

statements: Surah Al-Kahf has four main stories.
One concerns Musa and al-Khidr.
One concerns Yusuf and his brothers.
medium.explain: The story of Yusuf is in Surah Yusuf. Al-Kahf contains the cave sleepers, the two gardens, Musa and al-Khidr, and Dhul-Qarnayn.

statements: Surah Al-Kahf has 110 ayahs.
Surah Al-Isra has 111 ayahs.
Surah Yusuf has 101 ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah Yusuf has 111 ayahs, the same count as Al-Isra. Al-Kahf has 110.

statements: Juz 30 is commonly called Juz Amma.
Juz 30 begins with Surah An-Naba.
Juz 30 contains 36 surahs.
hard.explain: Juz 30 runs from Surah An-Naba (78) to An-Nas (114), which is 37 surahs, not 36.

statements: The first revelation was the opening verses of Surah Al-Alaq.
Surah Al-Muddaththir came early, after the pause in revelation.
Surah Al-Fatihah was the first revelation.
hard.explain: The first revelation was Surah Al-Alaq, verses 1–5, at the cave of Hira. Al-Fatihah was revealed early in the Makkan period but was not the first.

statements: Surah Ar-Rahman repeats one verse 31 times.
That repeated verse asks which of the favours of your Lord you would deny.
Surah Ar-Rahman is part of juz 30.
hard.explain: Surah Ar-Rahman is surah 55 and falls in juz 27. Its refrain is repeated 31 times.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ passed away in 11 AH.
Abu Bakr's caliphate lasted roughly two years.
Umar's caliphate lasted roughly two years.
hard.explain: Umar's caliphate lasted about ten years, from 13 AH to 23 AH. Abu Bakr's was the short one, roughly two years.

statements: Surah At-Tawbah is the only surah that does not open with the Basmalah.
The Basmalah appears within Surah An-Naml.
Surah At-Tawbah is the shortest surah in the Qur'an.
hard.explain: Surah At-Tawbah has 129 ayahs and is one of the longer surahs. The shortest is Al-Kawthar, with three.

statements: Surah Al-Baqarah has 286 ayahs.
Surah Al-Imran has 200 ayahs.
Surah An-Nisa has 200 ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah An-Nisa has 176 ayahs. Al-Imran is the one with 200.

statements: Surah Al-An'am has 165 ayahs.
Surah Al-A'raf has 206 ayahs.
Surah Al-Ma'idah has 165 ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Ma'idah has 120 ayahs. It is Al-An'am that has 165.

statements: Surah Maryam is surah 19.
Surah Ta-Ha is surah 20.
Surah Al-Anbiya is surah 20.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Anbiya is surah 21. Surah 20 is Ta-Ha.

statements: Badr was fought in Ramadan of 2 AH.
Uhud was fought in 3 AH.
The conquest of Makkah took place in 6 AH.
hard.explain: The conquest of Makkah took place in Ramadan of 8 AH. The Treaty of Hudaybiyyah was the event of 6 AH.

statements: Mu'tah was fought in 8 AH.
Tabuk took place in 9 AH.
Khaybar took place in 9 AH.
hard.explain: Khaybar took place in 7 AH, shortly after the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.

statements: Abu Bakr's caliphate began in 11 AH.
Umar's caliphate began in 13 AH.
Uthman's caliphate began in 13 AH.
hard.explain: Uthman's caliphate began in 23 AH, after Umar's roughly ten-year rule.

statements: Surah Al-Kawthar has three ayahs.
Surah Al-Asr has three ayahs.
Surah An-Nasr has four ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah An-Nasr has three ayahs, like Al-Kawthar and Al-Asr.

statements: Juz 30 runs from An-Naba to An-Nas.
Juz 30 contains 37 surahs.
Juz 29 begins with Surah Al-Mulk, surah 68.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Mulk is surah 67, and juz 29 does begin with it. The surah number given is wrong; 68 is Al-Qalam.

statements: Surah Al-Fil refers to the Year of the Elephant.
Surah Quraysh follows Surah Al-Fil in the mushaf.
Surah Quraysh precedes Surah Al-Fil in the mushaf.
hard.explain: Al-Fil is surah 105 and Quraysh is surah 106, so Quraysh follows it.

statements: Surah Yusuf tells one continuous narrative.
Surah Yusuf has 111 ayahs.
Surah Yusuf is a Madinan surah.
hard.explain: Surah Yusuf is Makkan. It has 111 ayahs and is distinctive for telling a single sustained narrative.

statements: Al-Bukhari died in 870 CE.
Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj died in 875 CE.
Abu Dawud compiled one of the two Sahih collections.
hard.explain: The two Sahih collections are those of al-Bukhari and Muslim. Abu Dawud compiled a Sunan, one of the other four of the six books.

statements: Abu Hanifah died in 767 CE.
Malik ibn Anas died in 795 CE.
Al-Shafi'i died before Abu Hanifah.
hard.explain: Al-Shafi'i died in 820 CE, over fifty years after Abu Hanifah. The usual order is Abu Hanifah, Malik, al-Shafi'i, then Ahmad ibn Hanbal.

statements: Surah Ar-Rahman's refrain appears 31 times.
Surah Al-Mursalat also has a repeated refrain.
Surah Ar-Rahman is a surah of juz 30.
hard.explain: Surah Ar-Rahman is surah 55 and falls in juz 27. Al-Mursalat does have its own repeated refrain.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ passed away in Rabi al-Awwal.
The Hijrah took place in the month of Rabi al-Awwal.
The Hijri calendar begins its year with Rabi al-Awwal.
hard.explain: The Hijri year begins with Muharram. The calendar counts from the year of the Hijrah, but its first month is Muharram, not the month of the migration itself.

statements: Surah Al-Isra is also known as Bani Isra'il.
Surah Al-Isra has 111 ayahs.
Surah Al-Isra is also known as Surah Al-Mi'raj.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Isra (17) is also called Bani Isra'il. 'Surah Al-Mi'raj' is not one of its recognised names.

statements: Surah Al-Kahf is surah 18.
Surah Maryam is surah 19.
Surah Ta-Ha is surah 19.
hard.explain: Ta-Ha is surah 20, immediately after Maryam.

statements: Surah Al-Hajj contains a sajdah.
Surah As-Sajdah contains a sajdah.
Surah Al-Baqarah contains a sajdah.
hard.explain: Despite its length, Surah Al-Baqarah contains no verse of prostration.

statements: Khaybar was in 7 AH.
Hudaybiyyah was in 6 AH.
Hunayn was in 7 AH.
hard.explain: Hunayn was fought in 8 AH, shortly after the conquest of Makkah.

statements: Surah An-Naba has 40 ayahs.
Surah An-Nazi'at has 46 ayahs.
Surah Abasa has 60 ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah Abasa has 42 ayahs.

statements: Al-Nasa'i died in 915 CE.
Al-Tirmidhi died in 892 CE.
Al-Nasa'i died before al-Tirmidhi.
hard.explain: Al-Nasa'i outlived al-Tirmidhi by more than twenty years; he was the last of the six compilers to die.

statements: Surah Al-Imran has 200 ayahs.
Surah Al-Ma'idah has 120 ayahs.
Surah Al-Anfal has 120 ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Anfal has 75 ayahs.

statements: The Battle of Siffin was fought during Ali's caliphate.
The Battle of the Camel was fought during Ali's caliphate.
The Battle of Siffin was fought during Uthman's caliphate.
hard.explain: Both Siffin and the Battle of the Camel took place during the caliphate of Ali, in the period of civil conflict known as the first fitnah.

statements: Surah Al-Fath was revealed in connection with Hudaybiyyah.
Surah Al-Anfal relates largely to Badr.
Surah Al-Hashr relates largely to Badr.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Hashr concerns the exile of Banu al-Nadir, not Badr.

statements: Surah Yunus is surah 10.
Surah Hud is surah 11.
Surah Ibrahim is surah 13.
hard.explain: Surah Ibrahim is surah 14. Surah 13 is Ar-Ra'd.

statements: Malik ibn Anas compiled the Muwatta.
Ahmad ibn Hanbal compiled a Musnad.
Al-Shafi'i compiled the Muwatta.
hard.explain: The Muwatta is Malik's. Al-Shafi'i, who studied under Malik, is known for al-Risalah and al-Umm.

statements: The Hijri calendar was formally instituted during Umar's caliphate.
Its first year corresponds to 622 CE.
It was formally instituted during Abu Bakr's caliphate.
hard.explain: The calendar was formally established under Umar, who set its starting point at the year of the Hijrah.

statements: Surah Al-Waqi'ah is surah 56.
Surah Al-Hadid is surah 57.
Surah Ar-Rahman is surah 56.
hard.explain: Surah Ar-Rahman is surah 55, immediately before Al-Waqi'ah.

statements: Zayd ibn Thabit led the compilation under Abu Bakr.
He was also central to the standardisation under Uthman.
He was a Muhajir from Makkah.
hard.explain: Zayd ibn Thabit was from Madinah and so was among the Ansar, not the Muhajirun.

statements: Surah Al-Mulk has 30 ayahs.
Surah Nuh has 28 ayahs.
Surah Al-Jinn has 18 ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Jinn has 28 ayahs. Surah Al-Jinn and Surah Nuh both have 28.

statements: The Prophet ﷺ was born in the Year of the Elephant by the traditional account.
He was about forty at the first revelation.
He was about thirty at the first revelation.
hard.explain: The traditional account places the first revelation at about the age of forty.

statements: Surah Al-Ankabut is surah 29.
Surah Ar-Rum is surah 30.
Surah As-Sajdah is surah 31.
hard.explain: As-Sajdah is surah 32. Surah 31 is Luqman.

statements: Abu Hanifah is associated with Kufa.
Malik ibn Anas is associated with Madinah.
Ahmad ibn Hanbal is associated with Madinah.
hard.explain: Ahmad ibn Hanbal is associated with Baghdad. Malik is the one associated with Madinah.

statements: Surah Al-Qadr describes a night better than a thousand months.
Surah Al-Qadr has five ayahs.
Surah Al-Qadr is a Madinan surah.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Qadr (97) is generally classified as Makkan, though a minority view holds otherwise.

statements: Tabuk took place in 9 AH.
The Farewell Pilgrimage took place in 10 AH.
The Farewell Pilgrimage took place in 9 AH.
hard.explain: The Farewell Pilgrimage was in 10 AH, the year before the Prophet's passing in 11 AH.

statements: Surah Al-Fil has five ayahs.
Surah Quraysh has four ayahs.
Surah Al-Ma'un has four ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Ma'un has seven ayahs.

statements: Surah Al-Ahzab is surah 33.
It contains the verse naming the Prophet ﷺ the seal of the prophets.
It is a Makkan surah.
hard.explain: Al-Ahzab is Madinan; it relates to the Confederates who besieged Madinah at Khandaq.

statements: Surah Al-Anfal relates largely to Badr.
Surah At-Tawbah follows it in the mushaf.
Surah Al-Anfal has 129 ayahs.
hard.explain: Al-Anfal has 75 ayahs. It is At-Tawbah that has 129.

statements: Surah Qaf is surah 50.
Surah Sad is surah 38.
Surah Nun is the common name of surah 67.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Qalam, which opens with the letter Nun, is surah 68. Surah 67 is Al-Mulk.

statements: Al-Sab' al-Tiwal begins with Al-Baqarah.
Its seventh member is disputed.
It consists of nine surahs.
hard.explain: The name means 'the seven long ones'. The dispute concerns which surah occupies the seventh place.

statements: Ibn Khaldun wrote the Muqaddimah.
He died in 1406 CE.
He wrote Tafsir al-Qur'an al-Azim.
hard.explain: That tafsir is Ibn Kathir's. Ibn Khaldun is known for the Muqaddimah and his universal history.

statements: Surah Al-Mumtahanah is surah 60.
Surah As-Saff is surah 61.
Surah Al-Hashr is surah 61.
hard.explain: Al-Hashr is surah 59. As-Saff is 61.

statements: Zayd ibn Thabit was of the Ansar.
He led the compilation under Abu Bakr.
He was among the Muhajirun.
hard.explain: He was from Madinah, and so of the Ansar rather than the emigrants from Makkah.

statements: The Saqifah gathering followed the Prophet's passing.
It concluded with allegiance to Abu Bakr.
It concluded with allegiance to Umar.
hard.explain: Abu Bakr was given the pledge at the Saqifah. Umar succeeded him two years later.

statements: Surah Muhammad is surah 47.
It is also called Surah al-Qital.
It is the only surah named after a prophet.
hard.explain: Six surahs are named after prophets. Surah Muhammad is the only one named after the Prophet ﷺ himself.

statements: Al-Mufassal is the final portion of the mushaf.
Scholars differ over where it begins.
Al-Mufassal is the opening portion of the mushaf.
hard.explain: Al-Mufassal is the concluding section of shorter surahs. The opening section is al-Sab' al-Tiwal.

statements: Muhkam and mutashabih are mentioned in Surah Al-Imran.
Muhkam verses are clear in meaning.
Mutashabih verses are the clear ones.
hard.explain: It is the reverse: muhkam are the clear verses, mutashabih those admitting more than one reading.

statements: Surah Al-Hujurat is surah 49.
Surah Qaf is surah 50.
Surah Adh-Dhariyat is surah 52.
hard.explain: Adh-Dhariyat is surah 51. Surah 52 is At-Tur.

statements: Abu Sufyan commanded at Uhud.
He accepted Islam at the conquest of Makkah.
He was killed at Badr.
hard.explain: Abu Jahl was killed at Badr. Abu Sufyan lived on and accepted Islam in 8 AH.

statements: Surah Ar-Ra'd is surah 13.
Surah Ibrahim is surah 14.
Surah Al-Hijr is surah 16.
hard.explain: Al-Hijr is surah 15. Surah 16 is An-Nahl.

statements: The first fitnah included Siffin.
It fell within Ali's caliphate.
It fell within Uthman's caliphate.
hard.explain: The first fitnah followed Uthman's killing and unfolded during Ali's caliphate.

statements: Surah Al-Fath has 29 ayahs.
It refers to Hudaybiyyah as a clear victory.
It has 129 ayahs.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Fath has 29 ayahs. At-Tawbah is the surah with 129.

statements: The Ridda campaigns took place under Abu Bakr.
They included the Battle of Yamamah.
They took place under Umar.
hard.explain: The Ridda campaigns fell within Abu Bakr's short caliphate, 11–13 AH.

statements: Surah Al-Ma'arij is surah 70.
Surah Nuh is surah 71.
Surah Al-Muzzammil is surah 72.
hard.explain: Al-Jinn is surah 72. Al-Muzzammil is 73.

statements: Surah Al-Insan is also called Surah Ad-Dahr.
Surah Al-Mursalat is surah 77.
Surah Al-Insan is surah 75.
hard.explain: Surah Al-Insan is surah 76. Surah 75 is Al-Qiyamah.

statements: Umar instituted the Hijri calendar.
Its year one corresponds to 622 CE.
Its year one corresponds to the year of the Prophet's birth.
hard.explain: The calendar counts from the year of the Hijrah, 622 CE, not from the Prophet's birth around 570 CE.

events.text: The first revelation at the cave of Hira

easy.explain: The first revelation came around 610 CE. The migration to Madinah followed about twelve years later, in 622 CE.

events.text: The birth of the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ

easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ was born around 570 CE. Makkah was conquered peacefully in 8 AH, 630 CE, around sixty years later.
The Hijrah was in 622 CE and the Farewell Pilgrimage in 10 AH, 632 CE, shortly before the Prophet ﷺ passed away.

events.text: The passing of the Prophet ﷺ

easy.explain: Badr was fought in 2 AH, 624 CE. The Prophet ﷺ passed away in 11 AH, 632 CE.
The Year of the Elephant is traditionally placed around the year of the Prophet's birth, about forty years before the first revelation.

events.text: The first revelation at the cave of Hira

easy.explain: Revelation began around 610 CE. Makkah was entered peacefully twenty years later, in 8 AH.
Masjid Quba was built on arrival in Madinah at the very start of the Madinan period. The Farewell Pilgrimage came nine years later, shortly before the Prophet's passing.

events.text: The Prophet ﷺ receives his first revelation
The Prophet ﷺ passes away in Madinah

easy.explain: Around twenty-two years separate the first revelation from the Prophet's passing in Madinah.

events.text: The caliphate of Uthman ibn Affan begins

easy.explain: Badr was fought in the second year after the Hijrah; Uthman became caliph twenty-one years later.
A group of Muslims first sought refuge in Abyssinia around 615 CE, some seven years before the migration to Madinah.

events.text: The birth of the Prophet ﷺ

easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ was around fifty-two at the time of the Hijrah.

events.text: The caliphate of Abu Bakr begins

easy.explain: Hudaybiyyah came five years before the Prophet's passing and the accession of Abu Bakr.
The Year of the Elephant is traditionally placed around the Prophet's birth, some fifty-four years before Badr.
Around seventeen years passed between the start of public preaching in Makkah and the city's peaceful conquest.

events.text: The change of qiblah to the Ka'bah

easy.explain: The qiblah was changed early in the Madinan period; Tabuk was the last major expedition, seven years later.
The Prophet ﷺ married Khadijah around fifteen years before the first revelation came to him at the cave of Hira.
The Prophet ﷺ was about thirty-five when he settled the Quraysh dispute over placing the Black Stone, some seventeen years before the Hijrah.
The night journey took place in the final Makkan years, about a decade before Makkah was entered peacefully.
Seven years separate Uhud from the Farewell Pilgrimage, which came shortly before the Prophet's passing.
Thirty-four years separate the migration from the beginning of Ali's caliphate.
The siege of Madinah at Khandaq came four years before the expedition to Tabuk, the last the Prophet ﷺ led in person.

events.text: The passing of the Prophet ﷺ

easy.explain: Abu Bakr and Umar led in the twelve years between the Prophet's passing and Uthman's accession.
About eighteen years separate the beginning of revelation from the truce at Hudaybiyyah.

events.text: The boycott of Banu Hashim begins

easy.explain: The Makkan boycott preceded the Hijrah; Badr was fought two years after the migration.
The Prophet ﷺ was around forty-three when the call became public, three years after the first revelation.

events.text: The caliphate of Abu Bakr begins

easy.explain: Three years separate the conquest of Makkah from the Prophet's passing and Abu Bakr's accession.
Five years separate Badr from Khaybar, which followed the Treaty of Hudaybiyyah.

events.text: The caliphate of Hasan ibn Ali

easy.explain: Twenty-seven years and three caliphates separate the start of Umar's rule from Hasan's brief caliphate.
Al-Bukhari belongs to the third Islamic century; Ibn Kathir, the mufassir and historian, to the eighth.
Abu Hanifah is the earliest of the four school founders; al-Ghazali lived more than three centuries later.

events.text: The change of qiblah to the Ka'bah

easy.explain: The qiblah changed early in the Madinan period, eight years before the Farewell Sermon.
The pledge that enabled the Hijrah came shortly before the migration; Uhud followed three years later.
The flight to Abyssinia belongs to the years of persecution in Makkah; Tabuk came fifteen years later.
The Year of Sorrow, with the loss of Khadijah and Abu Talib, came about eleven years before tribes began arriving in Madinah in numbers.
Masjid Quba was built on arrival in Madinah; Hunayn was fought seven years later, just after the conquest of Makkah.

events.text: The compilation of the Qur'an under Abu Bakr
The standardisation of copies under Uthman

easy.explain: The written collection was gathered under Abu Bakr; standard copies were produced and distributed under Uthman more than a decade later.
Umar accepted Islam during the Makkan years of persecution, about eighteen years before becoming caliph.

events.text: The passing of the Prophet ﷺ

easy.explain: Mu'tah was fought three years before the Prophet's passing, earlier in the same year as the conquest of Makkah.
Khadijah died about five years before Badr, in the Year of Sorrow.
Umar accepted Islam during the Makkan persecution, about fourteen years before Makkah was entered.
Six years separate Uhud from Tabuk, the last expedition the Prophet ﷺ led in person.
About twenty-six years separate the first revelation from the decisive battle in Syria under Umar.
Four years separate the truce at Hudaybiyyah from the Farewell Pilgrimage.

events.text: The caliphate of Abu Bakr begins

easy.explain: Twenty-four years and two caliphates separate the first and fourth of the Rashidun.
Three years separate the siege of Madinah from Hunayn, fought just after the conquest of Makkah.
About eleven years separate the start of the public call from the first major battle.

events.text: The passing of the Prophet ﷺ

easy.explain: Al-Bukhari compiled his collection more than two centuries after the Prophet's passing.
More than five centuries separate the founder of the Maliki school from Ibn Taymiyyah.
The five daily prayers were prescribed at the Mi'raj, before the Hijrah; the qiblah changed afterwards, in Madinah.

events.text: The standardisation of the Qur'an under Uthman

easy.explain: The losses at Yamamah prompted the first written compilation; the standardisation of copies came more than a decade later.
About twenty-seven years separate the marriage from the migration.

events.text: The martyrdom of Husayn at Karbala

easy.explain: Fifty-three years separate Mu'tah, in the Prophet's lifetime, from Karbala.
Eighteen years and two caliphates separate Uthman's accession from the beginning of Umayyad rule.

events.text: The Prophet ﷺ is orphaned of his mother Aminah

easy.explain: The Prophet ﷺ lost his mother at about six years of age, some thirty-four years before revelation began.

events.text: Hamza ibn Abd al-Muttalib accepts Islam
